# Awesome Loop

> Looped and recurrent-depth language models. Each deep card records the loop layout, what the main comparison holds fixed, the paper's results with table or figure references, and caveats taken from the paper. All numbers are author-reported; nothing is converted or extrapolated. Comparison keys: params = unique parameters, active-params = active parameters, flops = training FLOPs, kv = KV cache per token, tokens = training tokens, depth = executed layers per token, wallclock = wall-clock time.

## Deep cards

- [LoopRes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.31094.md): Finetune a pretrained LLM into a prelude-core-coda loop whose core layers attend over the block outputs of the previous loop, with a trained loop-aware key on each source. Layout: L0-6 (7 layers) -> [L7-20 (14 layers)] x 3 or 7 -> L21-27 (7 layers); injection depth-attention; KV per-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth, kv.
- [GLM-5.4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/zai-glm-5-4.md): Z.ai turns 28 layers of its pre-trained GLM-5 base into a two-pass loop through continued training at the 750B scale, with per-token gates, a shared-plus-sliding-window KV cache and reused sparse-attention indices. Layout: earlier layers (layer count not stated) -> [28 shared layers (28 layers)] x 2 -> later layers (layer count not stated); injection gated; KV first-pass. Held fixed: params; differs: flops.
- [Inkling 2 Mini](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/tml-inkling-2-mini.md): Open-weight MoE (26.4B total, 3.4B active) that runs the middle 12 of its 24 layers three times with shared weights, released with a variable-loop research twin used to measure how pass count affects capability and CoT monitorability. Layout: L0-5 (6 layers) -> [L6-17 (12 layers)] x 3 -> L18-23 (6 layers); injection depth-attention; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops; differs: none.
- [Looped CED](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.13378.md): Loop the CED encoder layers that produce global KV, train with random depth, and keep only the last round's KV. Layout: L0-1 (2 layers) -> [L2-5 (4 layers)] x max(1, Poisson(8)) -> L6-11 (6 layers); injection gated; KV last-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens, kv; differs: flops, depth.
- [LoopDuet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2611.07211.md): Serve looped Transformers with fewer core loops for ordinary prompt tokens than for the last prompt token and the decoded tokens, run the deep tail as a compact batch in vLLM, and lower prefilling depth when the queue grows. Layout: prelude 4 layers -> [core 6 layers] x 32 (OLMo r32 checkpoint) -> coda 4 layers; injection n/a; KV last-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens, kv; differs: depth, wallclock.
- [SMELT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2609.01343.md): With per-token FLOPs, total parameters and KV cache matched, looping the middle half of an MoE Transformer twice lowers loss at four scales up to 54B non-embedding parameters and saves 6.8-18.0% of training FLOPs on the fitted frontier. Layout: L1-3 (3 layers) -> [L4-9 (6 layers)] x 2 -> L10-12 (3 layers); injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops, params, kv, tokens; differs: active-params, depth.
- [Parcae](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2604.12946.md): Constrain the loop's injection to a stable negative-diagonal form, sample depth per sequence, and fit training and test-time scaling laws for looping at fixed parameter count. Layout: prelude 8 layers -> [core 8 layers] x Poisson with mean 8, per sequence -> coda 8 layers; injection gated; KV n/a. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth.
- [YOCO-U](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2604.01220.md): Loop only YOCO's self-decoder, whose layers use sliding-window attention, so extra depth costs compute while the cross-decoder's global KV is still computed once. Layout: [Universal Self-Decoder, SWA-512 (10 layers)] x 3 -> Cross-Decoder, shared global KV (10 layers); injection none; KV single-global. Held fixed: params, active-params, flops; differs: tokens, depth, kv.
- [Retrofitted Recurrence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2511.07384.md): Turn pretrained 1B models into prelude-core-coda recurrent models by dropping middle layers and looping a block, then keep training while a curriculum raises the mean recurrence. Layout: L0-3 (4 layers) -> [L10-17 (8 layers)] x Poisson-Lognormal, mean ramped to 4, 8, 16 or 32 -> L18-21 (4 layers); injection concat; KV n/a. Held fixed: tokens; differs: params, flops, depth.
- [Ouro (LoopLM)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2510.25741.md): Pre-train a weight-tied layer stack that repeats 4 times, with a learned exit gate, on 7.7T tokens; the authors report that the 1.4B and 2.6B models match dense models of up to 12B parameters. Layout: [whole stack (2.6B: 48 layers) (24 layers)] x 8 in Stage 1a, then 4; injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: none; differs: params, tokens.
- [PLT](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2510.24824.md): Run loop l of token i in the same forward pass as loop l+1 of token i-1, let later loops reuse the first loop's KV plus a gated SWA, and a looped model decodes at close to unlooped latency and KV. Layout: [all layers, every loop (100% of layers)] x 2 or 3 (PLT-2 / PLT-3); injection additive; KV first-pass. Held fixed: params, active-params, tokens; differs: flops, depth, kv.
- [MoR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2507.10524.md): Routers give each token its own number of passes through a shared middle block, and each pass caches KV only for its active tokens; at equal training FLOPs MoR beats fixed-depth recursive baselines and often vanilla, with fewer parameters. Layout: first layer (1 layer) -> [shared block (10 layers)] x 1-3 per token, set by the router (Nr=3) -> last layer (1 layer); injection none; KV per-pass. Held fixed: flops; differs: params, tokens, depth, kv.
- [Huginn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/2502.05171.md): Pretrain a 3.5B prelude-core-coda transformer with a randomly sampled number of core iterations, so test-time compute scales by iterating the core more. Layout: P (2 layers) -> [R (4 layers)] x log-normal Poisson, mean 32 -> C (2 layers); injection concat; KV per-pass. Held fixed: params, tokens; differs: flops, depth.

## Other papers

- [Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32802): After each window of context, a Transformer LM 'sleeps', rerunning its whole network N-1 more times over that window with each pass's output fed into the next and merging the new keys and values into the cache through a learned gate, while decoding between windows stays one pass per token; on held-out code, the N=4 model matches the no-sleep baseline's loss with 2.39× fewer in-context tokens. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-24.
- [The Teacher Is Already Inside: Self-Distilling Looped Language Models Beyond Their Last Loop](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32452): ELPSD post-trains the looped LM Ouro-1.4B-Thinking, which runs one shared stack four times per token, by distilling its last loop on its own rollouts towards a frozen copy's next-token distribution extrapolated from loop 1 through loop 4; without any reward, the average avg@8 over five math benchmarks rises from 61.15 to 63.69. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-24.
- [LoopFit: Retrofitting Pretrained Diffusion Transformers with Recurrent Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32175): LoopFit retrofits the pretrained pixel-space MiniT2I diffusion transformer to repeat its middle blocks within each denoising step, scaling and shifting each patch's attention input by that patch's feature change in the previous pass and up-weighting patches whose errors persist; across 12 visual puzzle settings it solves 89.8% of boards, against 87.8% for SelfCondFM. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-24.
- [LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.32067): LoopDVR converts pretrained EdgeCrafter detection, segmentation and pose models into looped networks that share one Transformer block within each group of similar consecutive layers in the ViT backbone and the query decoder, adding a per-layer Loop Adapter; on COCO val2017, LoopDet-S reaches 50.9 box AP with 7.0M parameters, against 51.7 AP with 9.8M for the reference ECDet-S. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-24.
- [Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31977): Dooop distills a pretrained diffusion transformer into a looped student whose shared middle blocks start from teacher blocks, training each loop's output as one fixed-point step toward the teacher and treating each loop as a step of an ODE in depth, so the loop count is chosen at inference; on SD3-medium, the 0.756B student with two loops scores 0.661 on GenEval against 0.648 for the 2.03B teacher. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-24.
- [Beyond the Last Loop: Reinforcement Learning with a Teacher Extrapolated from the Model Itself](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31939): ELGO adds to GRPO a dense per-token distillation term that pulls the last loop of Ouro-1.4B-Thinking towards a teacher extrapolated from loop 1 through loop 4 of a frozen anchor copy, which is replaced by the current model once the student's KL to the teacher falls below a threshold; the average avg@8 over five math benchmarks rises to 64.20, against 62.32 for GRPO. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-24.
- [How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31513): Shows that additive input injection, which feeds the encoded query into every iteration of a recurrent-depth model, is exactly Halpern iteration, proves that a slowly vanishing step size converges with a truncated-backpropagation window polylogarithmic in depth, and turns the required Lipschitz constraints into the Sparrow optimizer; in a small looped model whose core layer is iterated N times, Sparrow lowers final validation loss relative to Muon by 0.012–0.027 for every N and truncation window. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [SwiftLoop: Selective Refinement for Adaptive Implicit Reasoning in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31481): SwiftLoop learns from hindsight labels (K/V reusability or functional impact on the output) which latent positions of a looped Transformer can stop being refined, and freezes them while active positions keep attending to their cached K/V; on CODI-style LOTUS-1B it reaches 58.83% GSM8K accuracy with 1.80 loops per latent instead of six. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [Attention Latent Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31154): Attention Latent Feedback lets every sublayer attend over the previous token's outputs at its own depth and above, and adds a projection of the previous top-layer state to the token embedding, training with two parallel passes and decoding in one pass; on MoE-4.0B it raises average accuracy on seventeen downstream tasks from 45.1% to 47.0%. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30844): DyLoMo-DiT runs the weight-shared middle layers of a sparse-MoE diffusion Transformer three times at low noise and once at high noise, spending the saved parameters on more experts; on ImageNet 256x256, DyLoMo-DiT-XL reaches FID 4.22 against 5.57 for DiT-XL/2 at matched parameters and compute. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-23.
- [A Pipeline-Parallel System for Depth-Recurrent Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30581): Loop-PP is a pipeline-parallel training system for looped Transformers whose shared layer stack is split across stages, so each micro-batch revisits the same stages; it schedules each visit separately and keeps one copy of the shared weights, and on full-loop MoE models of 8B to 60B it uses up to 32.8% less peak memory than unrolled and weight-tied pipeline baselines. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [Test-Time Latent Computation to Improve Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30480): Lobals, a training-free decoding method for multimodal LLMs, feeds the penultimate-layer hidden state back into the contiguous layer window with the strongest attention to visual tokens and runs that window again before the final layer; on Qwen3-VL-8B it raises the average score over six benchmarks from 76.77 to 78.13. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [PackLoop: Row-Packed Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models under Concurrency](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30205): PackLoop speeds up concurrent self-speculative decoding of looped LMs by speculating only inside rows (one request on one loop) that already read that loop's KV cache; it is exact in FP32, and across 164 load points it beats the best existing schedule at 161 (median 1.25x, up to 1.76x). Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [The Temporal Residual: Fast and Effective Retrofitting of Latent Feedback into Pretrained Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29843): The temporal residual adds a second residual stream that every sublayer reads and writes and whose final state starts the same stream at the next token; retrofitted onto Qwen3.5-4B-Base with 5B tokens of training, it beats a standard model trained on the same data by 13 points on AIME 2025. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-23.
- [Hierarchical Reasoning Action Head for Tiny Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29813): HR-AH, an action head for a tiny VLA, runs the backbone once and then iterates three attention blocks over a fast low-level action state and a slower vision-grounded planning state, halting at inference once its predicted action chunk changes by less than a threshold; with a 22.5M-parameter head on a 0.5B backbone it reaches a 97.0% average success rate on LIBERO. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-22.
- [Loop-Count Schedules in Looped Transformers: An Empirical Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29704): Training looped Transformers with learned residual gates under three loop-count schedules shows the lower bound decides: R sampled from {1,...,6} collapses the gates to 0.1-0.5, while R from {2,3,4} keeps them at 0.6-0.9 and gives the best model, 2.909 nats versus 2.951 for a parameter-matched plain model. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-22.
- [MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29462): MoR4Rec, a sequential recommender, puts a shared Transformer block between unique input and output layers and lets a learned router choose how many times each item in a user's history passes through it, refreshing cached keys and values only for items still recursing; on MovieLens 1M it reaches 0.2377 Recall@5, against 0.2268 for the strongest baseline, LRURec. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-22.
- [loopxDINO: Dense Visual Prediction via Iterative Latent Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29180): loopxDINO replaces a stacked segmentation decoder on a frozen DINOv2-Base with one weight-tied cross-attention block that refines learned queries over T iterations and feeds intermediate masks back as attention biases; on Pascal VOC 2012 it reaches 85.66% mIoU at T=2 with 14.85M trainable parameters, against 84.57% for a 54.06M six-layer decoder. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-22.
- [What Makes Recurrence Generalize Across Lengths?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.29171): On state tracking, recurrent Transformers extrapolate with atomic operation tokens, while multi-token templates and absolute positional encoding limit them; scaling the recurrent operator reaches 35.1% exact match on 20-40 operations after training on 2-10, where larger fixed-depth Transformers stay at 0%. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-11-22.
- [When Wrong Answers Remain Unsettled: Failure Dynamics in Recurrent Reasoners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28971): When a trained 27M-parameter HRM on Sudoku-Extreme runs its weight-tied recurrence for one more 16-segment budget, 0.95 of solved answers persist but only 0.18 of wrong ones, so at this horizon most failures are still changing rather than trapped; the solved-above-wrong ordering also holds for a second seed, TRM, Maze, GRAM-guided TRM and N-Queens. Category: understanding; focus: related; 2026-11-21.
- [When do stored facts become available in looped transformers?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28808): Under final-loop supervision, looped Transformers expose stored synthetic facts progressively, later under heavier memorization loads but earlier than equal-depth untied models; in multi-hop chains, entity patches redirect downstream entities and the answer, while same-entity patches keep it in over 99.5% of tested cases. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-11-21.
- [R2WM: Recursive Reasoning Wireless Model for Long-Horizon mmWave Beam Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28774): R2WM follows TRM's nested schedule, reusing one backbone of two causal-attention blocks to update a latent state and a prediction state over a fixed history of beam indices and AoDs before decoding the next 10 beams at once; on DeepMIMO the 7.016M-parameter model reaches an average normalized beamforming gain of 0.9597, against 0.8629 for the GPT-2-based PaP-LLM. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-21.
- [Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28603): Gives distilled students extra computation at fixed backbone size, either by looping the whole stack with shared weights or by feeding the previous token's final-layer state back into every layer; converting Qwen2.5-0.5B to the cross-token recurrent form during on-policy distillation from a 7B teacher gives 57.5% on GSM8K, against 53.7% for the vanilla student distilled the same way. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-21.
- [LoopSight: Looped Vision Transformers with Gated Prediction Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28575): LoopSight loops a weight-shared ViT core on ARC grids and decodes from a gated prediction memory kept separate from the evolving hidden state, training at loop counts sampled from a truncated Gaussian; LoopSight-Small reaches 67.4% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1, against 60.8% for a reproduced LoopViT-Small. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-21.
- [Model Carving: Training Transformers That Optimize Their Own Topology](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27962): Puts learnable scalar gates on every sublayer of standard and looped Transformers so training removes the unneeded ones; carved models reach lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-11-20.
- [Mixture of Latent Recursions for Low-Rank Adaptation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27823): MoLR recursively refines each token's LoRA down-projected latent with one shared transformation, and a threshold router decides per token whether to recurse again; fine-tuning Llama-3.2-3B on reasoning tasks, it averages 61.21 versus 59.21 for LoRA with negligible parameter overhead. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-20.
- [Circular Predictive Coding Unlocks Effective Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27610): Closes a shallow predictive coding network into a loop, so energy relaxation keeps cycling through the same few layers to a fixed point equivalent to a deep equilibrium model, trained with local equilibrium propagation; with one causal Transformer block as the loop, it reaches 12.96 validation perplexity on TinyStories, against 13.33 for the same model trained with DEQ implicit gradients. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-20.
- [Loop-OPF: Solver-Informed Learning for Optimal Power Flow with Inference-Time Topology Adaptivity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27013): Loop-OPF builds its layers from primal-dual hybrid gradient iterations for DC-OPF, learns PDHG parameters without solution labels and trains as a DEQ, so its fixed point is optimal and feasible; one trained model adapts to unseen outages on IEEE 300-bus and PEGASE 1354-, 2869- and 9241-bus networks. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-20.
- [GLiDE: A Fast, Calibrated Decision Model Distilled from Reasoning Teachers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26509): Converts Qwen hybrid LMs into single-pass decision models via bidirectional full attention and multi-teacher distillation; checkpoint averaging plus parameter-free recurrent depth (reapplying middle layers) raises the 27B hidden-set score from 71.52 to 73.37. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-19.
- [dLoop: Looped Diffusion Language Models via Recurrent Latent Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26275): Restructures a pretrained diffusion language model into a Prelude-Loop-Coda design that reapplies a shared middle block before tokens are committed, reaching the highest or tied-highest accuracy on GSM8K, MATH, MBPP and HumanEval. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-19.
- [LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25595): LoopedWAM loops a shared six-block core in each expert of a robot world action model, and elastic self-distillation lets one checkpoint serve several action-depth and sampling-step budgets; it reaches 96.1% success on LIBERO. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-19.
- [Fold the Loop: Decoding-Time KV Memory for Looped Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25369): FoldCache lets groups of recurrent steps in a looped VLM share the group's final visual KV during decoding; on LoopVL it approximately halves prefix KV memory while matching full-cache accuracy on five open-ended benchmarks. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-19.
- [Late Entry in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24576): Late entry lets new tokens in looped language models skip early passes and run only the final passes over a deep context cache, outperforming matched early exit; Wake verification reaches 5.2x greedy-exact speedup on Ouro-2.6B. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-18.
- [LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.24301): Proposes LoopCache, self-speculative decoding for long-context looped Transformers that updates drafts across intermediate loops by confidence and rotates loop-specific KV caches; reports average 10.25x and 14.56x speedup over WFD and LoopSpec. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-18.
- [Simpler Tiny Recursive Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23677): STRM simplifies TRM to a single uniformly updated state, using jittered-rate exponential moving updates and slow-channel readout; under TRM's data, parameters and compute it gains 3.8 points on Sudoku-Extreme and matches TRM on Maze-Hard. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-18.
- [SenseNova-Loop-9B: Deeper Computation with Fewer Parameters](https://huggingface.co/sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B): Model card for SenseNova-Loop-9B, a multimodal model of approximately 9B parameters (text and images in, text out) that runs decoder layers 4-27 twice with shared weights and two-stream mHC residual mixing, so 32 stored layers give 56 layer executions; in a loop-scaling study with matched training and inference loops, 3 or 4 loops gave the best results. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-17.
- [Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23446): Besides adding gated attention adapters to EfficientNet-B0, the paper shares weights across repeated MBConv blocks with pass-specific BatchNorm; alternating two shared templates in Stage 6 ([B1, A, B, A]) removes 10.9% of the parameters and reaches 70.92% ImageNet-1k top-1 after one epoch of continued training, against 72.76% for the unshared control. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-17.
- [LoopPrune: Recurrent Pruning for Looped Diffusion Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22757): LoopPrune prunes looped diffusion Transformers with one mask shared by every pass of the reused blocks, scoring units across all loop positions, reconstructing weights from inputs pooled over positions and recovering against the dense teacher; at 30% structured pruning, Looped-DiT B/16 keeps 93.14% of the dense model's six-benchmark average accuracy. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-17.
- [Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22737): Proves that a single stored target sets a loss floor for looped refiners (HRM, TRM) on puzzles with many answers; training each pass toward the nearest correct answer solves 98.8% of multi-answer Sudoku versus 2.5%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-17.
- [LoopZip: Visual Token Compression for Efficient Looped Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22728): LoopZip compresses visual tokens in looped vision-language models without training, selecting tokens by attention from two calls of the same shared layer; on LoopVL-1B it keeps 97.16% of the original performance at 50% pruning ratio. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-17.
- [InfuseLoop: Cross-Trajectory Latent Injection for Scalable Parallel Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.22426): Adds cross-trajectory latent injection to Parallel Looped Transformers, so each loop aggregates causally available hidden states from later trajectories via attention residuals; this eliminates training-loss spikes and improves validation-loss scaling up to eight loops. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-17.
- [Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21921): Baton looped transformers pass the intermediate entity to the second loop as a token embedding; trained only on answers, two variants almost solve held-out two-hop questions, but next-token training makes accuracy rise then decline. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-11-16.
- [Déjà-Events: Multi-view 3D Geometry with Event Cameras via Sparsity-Aware Adaptive Gating](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21302): Distils an event-camera 3D model from the RGB teacher Déjà View, which repeatedly applies one shared transformer block, and gates that block by event density; it has the lowest pointmap error among evaluated event-based methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-16.
- [Efficient Multi-View Generation with Iterative Global-Local Proxy Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20703): GLPA sends cross-view information in multi-view diffusion through compact proxies and refines them by reusing the same attention parameters within a denoising step; on FLUX, attention runs 2.65× faster than dense attention and reconstruction improves. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-16.
- [Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.20404): Tests latent feedback, which feeds each token's top-layer state into the next token's input, against compute-matched multi-epoch Transformers; it saves at most 48% of the compute and 47% of the unique data. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-11-16.
- [LoopSkim: Lossless Multi-Depth Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19896): Proposes lossless speculative decoding for looped LMs in which each loop's readout checks draft tokens copied from the context and only full-depth readouts commit; without training, its speedup averages 1.73x that of LoopSpec. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-15.
- [When Does Reusing Layers Help Multimodal Embeddings?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19827): Tests eleven loop designs for multimodal embeddings, proving that under forward-only attention repeated layers cannot make earlier image states query-dependent; on MMEB-V2 an added loop loses 0.46 points, while native recurrence gains +4.23 points. Category: understanding; focus: related; 2026-11-15.
- [LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19649): A training-free speculative decoding method for looped LLMs that puts multi-token suffix drafts and shallow-loop predictions in one draft tree; average speedup over greedy decoding is 5.85x on Ouro-2.6B and 5.13x on Huginn-3.5B. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-14.
- [Architectures and KV Replay for Depth-Recurrent Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19446): Studies how to cut decoding KV memory in depth-recurrent LMs: looped hybrids need frequent attention anchors, and training with recurrent KV replay lets iterations share KV states with performance close to separate per-iteration caches. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-14.
- [Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.19131): Uses constrained deep RL (TRPO-Lag) to jointly choose local or edge execution and the latent-reasoning convergence threshold of a recurrent-depth VLA, reaching up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success than benchmark constrained RL methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-14.
- [Folding Language Models into Themselves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18113): Concertina folds every N adjacent teacher layers into one shared block run N times with low-rank corrections; distilled from Qwen3-4B on 22B tokens, a 2.27B model retains 84% of the teacher averaged over eight benchmarks. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-11-13.
- [Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17309): CRAM, a learned Hopfield-Tank energy minimized at inference, solves 99.996% of Sudoku-Extreme and 100% of Maze-Unique test puzzles with training at least 1,000x faster than looped models; the authors call these benchmarks trivially solvable. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-12.
- [Rectified Looped Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16265): Feeds each loop a linear interpolation between the current state and the block's prediction; at matched depth this lowers perplexity versus a standard looped Transformer and keeps hidden-state norms more stable, with no extra parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-12.
- [One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14947): Reuses one Restormer block at every iteration of unrolled MRI reconstruction and beats PromptMR+ with about 1/9 of its parameters; shared transformer blocks match or beat distinct-weight ones, while shared CNN blocks do worse. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-11.
- [Depth as a Candidate Source: Portfolio Allocation for Recurrent Test-Time Scaling in Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12293): Shows deeper recurrence in a frozen Huginn can lose correct answers found at shallower depths, and proposes Depth Portfolio Allocation, which spreads a test-time budget across depths and expands oracle coverage at matched candidate counts. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-09.
- [WiFo-R: Wireless Foundation Model with Recurrent Channel Representation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.11275): Builds a wireless channel foundation model whose parameter-shared recurrent updates refine CSI features and add latent tokens; multi-depth pretraining trains intermediate states to reconstruct CSI, and selectable depth improves the accuracy-complexity trade-off. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-08.
- [Learning When to Think: Adaptive Internal Computation for Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.10822): AIC refines an RL policy's latent state with one residual MLP block reused at every depth and trains a halting head jointly with the action through PPO with an expected-depth penalty; capped at eight steps per decision, it averages 3.3 refinement steps across twelve tasks, and its mean reward beats the best fixed-depth policy on seven tasks and trails it on four. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-07.
- [The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.09436): Appends a learned refinement block (CRF-as-RNN, modern Hopfield or ConvGRU) to a segmentation backbone and iterates it on its own logits, re-anchored to the backbone's prediction at every step; on ARCADE with 10% Gaussian noise the Hopfield block at T=5 improves Dice by +17 pp over the U-Net, while clean-data Dice gains reach at most 1.4 pp. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-06.
- [Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08977): Learns an energy over latent reasoning states and makes each loop a gradient step on it, giving a stopping signal; reaches 99.9% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme with 345× less inference compute than the next-best model. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-06.
- [ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18696): ARC-VLN runs a shared-parameter language backbone recursively for aerial VLN, letting only visual tokens exit early; on OpenFly it has the lowest navigation error of the compared methods and reduces FLOPs and GPU memory. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-05.
- [AlterNet: Adaptive-Depth Mixture-of-Experts with Learned Halting for Elastic Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08741): AlterNet loops over a shared pool of shallow MoE experts, picked by a depth-aware router, with per-expert halt heads for early stopping, so depth adapts and can be cut without retraining; results are preliminary. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-11-05.
- [Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.08236): Replaces ViT self-attention with a separable sum-of-Gaussians operator, globally Lipschitz with fixed kernels, across discrete, looped and Neural ODE ViTs; in the looped setting it raises CIFAR-100 Top-1 accuracy by 5.4-8.1 points. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-05.
- [Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07736): RELOAD fine-tunes pretrained encoders or decoders with a damped loop over their middle block; looping improves accuracy and calibration, mostly on reasoning chains longer than in training, where encoders gain up to 23 points. - [BRIDGE: Bridging the Semantic Quantization Gap for Generative Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07425): For generative recommendation, BRIDGE adds latent reasoning, self-distillation and effort-aware recurrence, which runs a shared loop decoder more times at early Semantic ID levels; it improves Recall@10 and NDCG@10 on three Amazon benchmarks. - [Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07226): Loopback Transformer reads each shared-block update separately, using geometric decay for total update weight and attention to allocate it; it reaches lower validation loss than standard Transformers with 40-75% of their Transformer parameters. - [LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06835): Loops the decoder layers of a causal encoder-decoder, storing each token's KV only on its first visit; one model covers 3 to 21 layer executions per token and, with enough loops, beats a single-pass baseline. - [Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06206): Compares standard and looped Transformers under a 100M-word budget; text-only, a 12-layer stack repeated four times beats a 48-layer Transformer by 5.4 BLiMP points, but recurrence does not clearly mitigate the multimodal-training drop. - [Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05724): Lets a speculative-decoding drafter deepen uncertain guesses with extra passes of its shared block, run in parallel with the one-pass draft; this improves acceptance length by 5.3% to 10.2% and speedup by 3.5% to 9.2%. - [LoopVQ: Sub 1-bit KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05304): LoopVQ vector-quantizes the KV cache of looped transformers, coding channels of several loop steps jointly; with Ouro and Huginn at 0.5 bits per element, it outperforms KV vector quantization methods built for standard LLMs. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05234): ARLoop gives each layer of a looped transformer attention over earlier outputs across depth; sliding-window depth attention matches full history, and a 1.2B model trained on 0.5T tokens beats Huginn-3.5B on all evaluated tasks. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [What Sets the Serving Speed of Looped Language Models? Measurements and Optimizations Graded by Exactness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05150): Measures serving of looped LMs Ouro and Huginn-0125, grading optimizations by exactness; the many small kernels per token set the cost, and fusing them behind rounding fences raises throughput 1.11-1.59x with identical outputs. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-11-03.
- [Best-of-Depth: Learning Exploratory Dynamics in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04663): Best-of-Depth trains a looped Transformer's recurrent trajectory as a candidate set by minimizing prediction loss across depths; on N-Queens, coverage reaches 91.03% versus 45.75% for final-depth training. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-11-03.
- [LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04137): Chooses 4-bit, 2-bit or final-loop KV reuse for each (loop, layer) cell of Ouro from an offline profile; serving Ouro-1.4B, the LoopKV-M plan stores 35% less KV than KIVI-4 and sustains 1.7-2.2x its goodput. - [Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03998): Dory1.0-4B is a looped nGPT language model with elastic depth, pre-trained on 6 trillion tokens; more loops raise accuracy, and caching only last-loop KV keeps most gains at a non-looped KV footprint. - [Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.03526): Library of Layers uses a router to choose and order blocks from a global library at inference, covering dense, depth-recurrent and MoE designs; it is competitive with all three when pretrained on text. - [Solv3R: 3D Looped Transformer as a Multi-view Solver](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02857): Trains a looped transformer whose update operator, independent of the iteration count, keeps refining multi-view geometry from its current state, so one solver handles offline and incremental reconstruction, relocalization and streaming without task-specific training. - [When Does Adaptive Halting Win? Selection Rules Matter in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.02333): On a frozen Ouro-1.4B, pre-registered tests show the winner between a trained stability probe and Ouro's exit gate flips with the operating-point selection rule; the probe shows no demonstrated advantage over an untrained KL baseline. - [How Does Chain-of-Thought Supervision Teach Models to Reason? A Theoretical Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.01740): Studies an in-context linear-regression weight predictor trained on gradient-descent trajectories and run recursively beyond them; long-horizon reasoning has phase transitions in context length and training CoT budget, and overthinking splits into error accumulation and amplification. - [There Is No Free Loop: When Does Looping a Trained Model Pay for Its Inference Compute?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42030): Adds loops to pretrained Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models (0.8B to 9B) and compares them with equal-parameter and equal-FLOPs unlooped baselines; only the looped 0.8B model beats both, so post-pretraining loops pay only for small models. - [Where KV-Cache Error Lives in Looped Language Models: A Diagnostic Study of Ouro and Huginn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41825): Studies how KV and shared-weight quantization error changes next-token distributions in looped LMs Ouro and Huginn-0125; per unit of error, values carry 94% of diagonal Fisher mass, but keys dominate measured KL. - [ElTab: Elastically Looped Tabular Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41819): ElTab trains one looped tabular transformer with supervision at randomly sampled early exits; on 30 OpenML datasets it matches six depth-specific looped models and a 12-layer TabPFN-style baseline with 25% fewer inference FLOPs. - [UpLoop: Training Looped Transformers via Upcycling at No Extra Pretraining Compute](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41720): Grows a shallow Transformer by copying layers and spends the saved compute on looping a shared middle block, at matched parameters, tokens and FLOPs; the 1.3B model's 22-task average rises from 22.99 to 27.52. - [How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40325): In looped decoders up to 1B parameters, full-stack looping is best at fixed parameters and middle-block looping at fixed training FLOPs; per-loop low-rank adapters help, and a normalization fix recovers Parallel Loop Transformer quality. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-10-29.
- [CopyLoop: Fast Looped Transformer Decoding via Context Copying and Shallow Screening](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38822): CopyLoop, a training-free decoding algorithm for looped Transformers, proposes multi-token suffixes from repeated context, screens them at shallow recurrent depth and verifies at full depth, reaching 2.98x--10.70x speedups on Base models. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-28.
- [Deeper Backpropagation or More Updates? Training Looped Language Models Across Budgets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38422): Compares shorter and longer truncated-backprop windows for training looped language models at roughly equal training time; the advantage of shorter windows shrinks as training budgets grow, so the preferred window can change. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-28.
- [Compute Has Shape: Self-Morphing the Internal Computation of Frozen LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38382): SelfMorph trains a selector that picks, per input, whether a frozen LLM keeps its forward path, repeats a layer span or branches hidden states; this gives an 8.06% mean relative improvement on five in-distribution benchmarks. - [Think Twice: The Metis-1.6 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37903): Metis-1.6 technical report on Praxis and Logos, two from-scratch models that run a hybrid Mamba-2 and attention MoE stack twice per token; Logos averages 52.93 across 40 post-trained benchmarks, and the report documents training failures. - [LoopFold: Parallelizing Recurrent Depth in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35556): LoopFold runs several recurrent depths of a looped Transformer in parallel batches, using a predictor for later-loop inputs and a corrector for their outputs; versus a nine-loop vanilla model it cuts decoding latency by 46%. - [StateLoop: Persistent State for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35544): StateLoop gives each token a gated persistent state carried across looped-Transformer iterations and projected back into the backbone output; it lowers Pile perplexity versus vanilla looping, with a gap that grows with trained loop depth. - [Cross-Loop Query Handoff: How Later Loops Redirect Two-Hop Retrieval in the Ouro Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34639): Transplants attention queries between loops of Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B; loop-3 queries injected into loop 1 rescue 90% and 97% of synthetic two-hop loop-1 failures that loop 3 fixes, versus 24% and 21% with shuffled donors. - [Recursive CLIP: Vision-Language Distillation with Looped Transformer Blocks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34563): Trains and distills CLIP models with recursive encoders that apply N transformer blocks M times at fixed ViT-B depth; CLIP tolerates substantial recurrent block reuse, though the effect depends on the encoder and downstream task. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-25.
- [Recency Is the Wrong Axis: A Negative Result on Windowed Deepest-Plane KV Caching in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34436): Tests a KV policy for looped models that keeps every loop's plane for recent positions and shares the deepest plane elsewhere; across three models, sharing cost depends on late-loop convergence and position, not recency. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-25.
- [ScaleRLT: Exact Log-Probabilities and Fast Deferred Rollouts for Reinforcement Learning on Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34427): ScaleRLT removes the log-probability mismatch between deferred rollouts and the learner's dense pass in RL on looped transformers, using a stop-gradient hybrid that replays the rollout schedule bit for bit and keeps the dense gradient. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-25.
- [LoopGR: Parameter-Efficient Scaling for Generative Recommendation via Recurrent Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34157): For generative recommendation, LoopGR alternates a shared generative decoder with a lightweight context updater over recurrent depth and self-distills a low-budget student; it beats an encoder-decoder baseline while reducing model size by up to 52%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-25.
- [One Model, Two Paths: Balancing Single-Pass and Looped Performance in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33517): Adapts a pretrained model to support both single-pass and looped inference by reusing middle-layer weights, and shows joint weighted losses with frozen-model guidance reduce single-pass degradation while keeping looped gains over continued training. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-24.
- [LSTM-Style Looped Transformers with Shared KV Caches](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33360): An LSTM-style looped Transformer shares one KV cache across its recurrent core, cutting persistent cache sets from fifteen to four and, at width 1024, using 40.4% fewer parameters than an untied control; a consistency loss in the final 10% of training removes 81–89% of the continuation-loss penalty. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-23.
- [Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32492): Accordion, an MoE LLM, serves five inference budgets by repeating a fixed prefix of single layers in a middle window, sampling one budget per micro-batch; after 3.6T tokens, more depth lifts Accordion-6B-A0.5B's 37-task macro-average by 3.01 points, with the middle budget capturing 89% of the gain. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-10-23.
- [Do Halting Heads Really Save Compute in Looped Language Models?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32246): Pretraining looped LMs up to 1.3B parameters, the paper finds halting heads trained on a mix of all iterations predict under half the iterations while tokens still run almost every iteration, and in batched generation, which waits for the slowest token, a model without a head is almost as good at that cost. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-10-23.
- [Agreement rather than normalisation keeps depth reusable in looped language models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31943): Removing state normalisation between loop steps drops Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B to zero accuracy by the trained budget on a balanced binary task, yet 19M-parameter looped models trained without it are never worse and extrapolate better, pointing to train-inference loop agreement as what keeps depth reusable. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-22.
- [BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31633): BeNice! lets looped LMs share the final recurrence's KV cache with earlier recurrences by pairing stochastic-depth pretraining with post-training that broadcasts that cache into the first recurrence; in simulated long-context inference, throughput rises by up to 23.6% and p90 time-to-first-token falls by up to 83.6%. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-22.
- [How Depth Growth and Looping Shape In-Context Learning in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31421): Compares dense, depth-grown and looped language models up to 3B parameters plus controlled tasks; grown and looped models rely more on context, acquire ICL earlier and retain it more strongly than a full-depth dense reference, and lean more on induction-ranked heads for few-shot performance. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-22.
- [Loop to Look Better: Learning Adaptive Depth for Question-Guided Perception in Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30824): LoopLook loops a middle-to-late window of a pretrained VLM's vision encoder with question-conditioned modulation, a learned exit gate and token-wise Mixture-of-Looks over loop states; across four backbones it gains up to 8.6% on MMStar and 8.1% on HallusionBench while adding 5.1-6.5% to time to first token. - [Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30128): LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block in sequential recommenders, with a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary deciding exit or continue for every item; on public benchmarks with four backbone families it consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. - [Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30066): Looped UDLMs repeat a two-block slice of the denoiser in each denoising step, reaching the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on about 0.5 trillion tokens with up to 2.8x fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3x fewer on FineWeb-Edu, and up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity at matched NFE. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-21.
- [How Much Gradient Does Truncated Backprop Lose in Looped Transformers?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28871): Across nine looped LMs, the weight gradient lost by backpropagating through only the last k loops barely changes with loop count (within about 0.03 from 32 to 64 loops); on Ouro keeping two of four loops still loses 81% of the final output's gradient, and the lost share falls by 0.07-0.22 within 300 fine-tuning steps. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-20.
- [Copied, Mixed or Computed? Testing Latent Intermediate Values with Minimal Pairs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28498): With prompts that differ in one token, the paper shows that answer-position probes in two looped and two standard LMs may be reading copied inputs, and tests candidate values against copies, generic mixing and use; in looped Ouro-1.4B the tests find a small code of the unwritten intermediate whose use is unresolved. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-20.
- [Asymmetric Looped Transformers: Fixed Global Representations for an Iterative Decoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28489): AsymLoop runs a causal encoder once to produce per-layer Global KV fixed across iterations, while a weight-tied decoder loops and attends jointly to it and to Local KV from its evolving state; at 1B it lifts average zero-shot accuracy on seven commonsense benchmarks from 49.58% for Full Loop to 50.85%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-20.
- [HistoLoop: Iterative Contextual Inference with a Looped Transformer for Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28339): HistoLoop predicts spatial gene expression from H&E images by looping a shared spatial Transformer for 4 steps between pre- and post-spatial Transformers, rebuilding context from updated spot states at finer resolutions; on HEST-Bench HVG50 its macro-averaged PCC is 0.480 versus 0.435 for MoLF. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-20.
- [PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27628): PAR trains a looped Qwen2.5-0.5B so iteration k predicts the state after the first k operations, and rescales recurrent states to their first-iteration norms; trained on at most 32 swap-S_5 moves, it reaches 95.5% full-state accuracy at 512 moves, versus 55.7% reported for RLT and 0.8% for explicit chain of thought. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-20.
- [Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27598): Meta Experts are MoE experts shared by all layers instead of private to one layer; they lower cross-entropy loss and raise downstream accuracy, and with activated experts and expert granularity fixed the model matches Vanilla MoE using only 70-80% of the experts. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-20.
- [Exploring Recurrent-Depth Language Models for Multitask Clinical Text Processing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.27559): Jointly fine-tunes recurrent-depth LMs (Ouro fixed at four recurrent steps, and HRM-Text-1B) and Qwen3 baselines on 9 clinical NLP datasets; across 13 datasets Ouro-1.4B-Thinking beats Qwen3-1.7B on 11, and Ouro-2.6B-Thinking is competitive with Qwen3-8B on most tasks. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-20.
- [recAMPLIFY: Large-Scale Pretraining of Recursive Protein Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26747): recAMPLIFY pretrains a masked protein LM whose weight-tied Transformer core refines residue states between a prelude and a coda; with 155M unique parameters on the same 2T tokens as AMPLIFY-350M it raises fold accuracy by 22.5%, and Gated Mixture Recurrence cuts expected layer depth by up to 37%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-19.
- [Nested Shared-Operator Recursion on ARC-AGI-1: An Empirical Study of HRM, TRM and URM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26666): Adds to HRM, TRM and URM a persistent intermediate state that the same operator updates after repeated fast-state updates, at matched parameter counts; on ARC-AGI-1 under a single-GPU budget, the nested variants show no consistent advantage, and exact solving stays near zero for all configurations. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-19.
- [Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.26030): Over nearly 600 runs, a fitted scaling law for looped transformers favors full BPTT over truncation when forward and backward loops are jointly optimized; two fully trained loops get lower validation loss than the compute-optimal non-looped model with about 27% fewer non-embedding parameters and 8% more compute. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-10-19.
- [Internalizing Chain-of-thought into Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25998): Constructs constant-bit-size looped Transformers that apply one shared decoder block L times per generated token, reading per-iteration KV caches; simulating a time-t(n), space-s(n) Turing machine, they cut both context window and CoT tokens by a factor of L versus the unlooped queue-machine simulation. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-10-19.
- [Spherical Fixed-Point Reasoners: Adaptive Loop Halting on the Hypersphere](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25646): SFPRM runs FPRM's damped fixed-point loop of a weight-tied nGPT block on the unit hypersphere, so injection, damping and halting become geodesic operations with proven convergence; it reaches 96.6%, 87.9% and 59.1% test accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme, Maze-Hard and Mini-ARC, outperforming FPRM. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-19.
- [Dual-Slot: From Serial Loops to Parallel Slots in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25086): Dual-Slot runs a looped middle block's two loops as parallel latent and prediction slots, the latter adding the previous token's latent state, trained via Jacobi iterations; the 1B dense model cuts Pile validation perplexity from 7.25 to 7.00 and keeps 93.1-96.5% of vanilla decoding throughput. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-10-18.
- [P2N: Reusing Deep Representations for Greater Effective Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25076): P2N adds the previous token's middle-core output to the current token's core input, extending effective depth across tokens for one vector addition per decoding step, trained with parallel Jacobi updates; at 1.5B parameters it lifts GSM8K accuracy by over 10 percentage points at nearly unchanged decoding latency. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-10-18.
- [UpLoop: Upcycling Large Language Models with Gated Loop](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.25004): UpLoop upcycles a pretrained non-looped LLM by looping each selected middle layer locally, with learned hidden-wise gates on the attention and MLP residual writes of later loops; starting from Qwen3-4B Base with SFT, it improves the 20-benchmark average by 6.17% at R=3, past the common two-loop saturation. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-18.
- [Block Recursive Transformers for Structured Parameter Sharing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24998): Block Recursive Transformers split the shared core between independent first and last layers into contiguous blocks and repeat each block before moving to the next; in decoder-only models up to 1.7B parameters this improves validation NLL and downstream accuracy over static recursive sharing baselines. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-18.
- [Inside the Loop: A Mechanistic Study of Looped Transformers on Permutation Traversal](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24135): On directed permutation traversal, a four-layer block looped eight times solves the task in every seed while an identically trained untied transformer of equal effective depth never does; probing shows the looped model steps through intermediate nodes in a staircase that adapts to its iteration budget. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-16.
- [Looped GNNs Beyond Fixed Depth: Graph Size Generalization and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24112): Looped GNNs reuse a pretrained processor beyond its training depth to generalize to larger graphs; Loop-Freeze-Steer freezes the processor and trains a small controller between iterations, and synthetic tasks and chip placement show its accuracy–trainable-parameter trade-off. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-16.
- [ReLaDrift: Recurrent Language Generation via Drifting for Test-Time Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23225): ReLaDrift reuses one Drifting Model over rounds to draft from noise and refine in continuous latent space, trained with a sampled round count and a final-round-only loss; on Sudoku Hard and GSM8K it trades test-time compute for quality, competitive with or better than diffusion and flow LMs. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-16.
- [Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part I: Topology, Input Injection, Recurrent-State Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23036): Isolates loop placement, input injection and recurrent-state design in matched from-scratch looped LMs; a prelude-recurrent-coda Huginn-style design outperforms Ouro across all ten benchmarks at 730M parameters and 336B tokens, and the advantage transfers to MoE. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-16.
- [Causal Latent Workspaces for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22796): The causal latent workspace Transformer runs one shared block for four rounds; before each round every position writes gated vectors into prefix-specific latent slots and reads a content-addressed summary, giving the best mean held-out perplexity in five of six byte-level settings against five Transformer controls. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-10-16.
- [Retrofitting Recurrent Vision-Language Models from Pretrained Backbones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22075): Retrofits TinyLLaVA-1.4B into a recurrent VLM by pruning language-backbone layers and looping a subset of the rest through a linear adapter, recovered with three-stage training and distillation; it beats the unpruned baseline trained on the same recovery data while storing 23.3% fewer language parameters. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-15.
- [LoopAhead: Speculating Ahead for Faster Decoding in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21594): LoopAhead drafts several future tokens from a looped LM's early-loop states with a lightweight drafter, uses deeper-loop feedback to pause or continue branches, and lets the full-depth model verify, reaching up to 7.82x decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding while preserving the output distribution. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-15.
- [AdaLoop: Thinking with the Vision Encoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21323): AdaLoop loops a span of a VLM's frozen vision encoder, modulating the shared layers at each iteration with question-conditioned AdaLN; with matched data and optimizer updates, it beats standard fine-tuning and question-conditioned single-pass baselines on six VisRO tasks across three VLM families. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-15.
- [LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20951): LEV turns natively looped language models into decision models that score options after each loop step, training all steps jointly; a 2.6B LEV rises from 63.2% at depth one to 76.2% at depth four on JevBench, and a stopper fitted on unlabelled requests saves 15% to 24% of compute for under one point. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-10-14.
- [LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19975): In a looped MoE that visits its middle block twice, LatentLoop runs the first visit on a compressed sequence, shares only MoE weights across visits and widens the model; at 1.3B–7B it lowers validation NLL, with predicted compute savings of 19.0% and 7.9% over vanilla MoE and the looped baseline. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-14.
- [Learning to Compute Is Not Learning to Retain or Reuse in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19768): Separates computing, retaining and reusing answers in looped Transformers executing Mealy machines in context: models trained to answer at loop 32 keep only 22% of answers at loop 64 (99.8% when one random position is supervised), and freezing position k from loop k drops accuracy to 4–6%. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-14.
- [Test-Time Forecasting: Recurrent Depth Enables In-Context Dynamics Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19552): Linking linear attention to (extended) dynamic mode decomposition, shows looped transformers can emulate dynamical-system propagators in context; Test-Time Forecasting uses gradient-descent iterations as recurrent depth, and small models trained on ODEs and PDEs generalize to out-of-distribution dynamics. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-14.
- [Tiny Recursive Message Passing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18649): Applies TRM-style deep supervision, truncated recursion and deduction lattices to recursive message-passing networks; a 16k-parameter model reaches about 99% test accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme after about 10 minutes of H100 training, and models transfer zero-shot to larger N-queens and SAT instances. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-13.
- [Looped Reasoning Finishes Earlier Than You Think](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18174): Since slowly decaying oscillatory modes bottleneck convergence in looped reasoners, QRR adds an exact per-token phase-rotation symmetry to FPRM's recurrent Transformer block; it converges stably and faster in quotient space and matches or beats recent recurrent reasoners on Sudoku, Maze and Mini-ARC. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-13.
- [LoOPSD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Looped Teachers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18162): LoOPSD makes a teacher by searching for a contiguous layer block of the same LLM to run twice with unchanged weights, then distills its predictions on student-generated prefixes into the standard model over rounds; on GSM8K with a 400-token thinking budget, Qwen3-1.7B rises from 42.30% to 79.61%. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-13.
- [Monitoring latent reasoning in looped language models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18127): Five interpretability lenses on eight looped LMs from four families show carry-loop models (Ouro, LoopUS) predict best within their training depth and lose answers, language or refusals under noise, while re-read-loop models (Parcae, Rec-OLMo, Huginn) improve or plateau with more iterations and are unaffected by noise. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-13.
- [LoopREG: Representation Supervision Enables Test-Time Recurrent Depth in Diffusion Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17877): LoopREG reuses one diffusion Transformer block at the state that REG aligns to a pretrained visual encoder and adds visits at inference; on ImageNet 256 x 256 it lowers SiT-B/2 FID from 15.08 to 4.91 at 400K training steps, and in a checkpoint trained with two visits one extra visit improves FID from 14.71 to 5.34. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-13.
- [Resample the Answer: Where to Spend Test-Time Compute in Recursive Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16427): Gated Answer Resampling resamples the answer state y of a Tiny Recursive Model and restarts only puzzles its halting head rejects; with at most 64 restarts per puzzle and no training, it lifts TRM from 85.9% to 99.4% on Sudoku-Extreme and from 68.8% to 85.6% on Pencil Puzzle Bench validation. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-12.
- [Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16415): CDS reuses each feature-interaction block of an industrial short-video ranker over several iterations with an intra-iteration residual; compressed, it cuts trainable parameters by 26.6% and raises training throughput by 6.4% within 0.03% of baseline offline quality, mainly via lower synchronization cost. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-12.
- [LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16368): LoopQuant is a loop-aware PTQ framework for looped LMs that shares a quantization-friendly representation across loops and allocates activation precision per loop; on Ouro-2.6B its W4A4 surpasses all W4A8 baselines, cuts model memory by 65.3% and decodes 1.7 times faster than BF16. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-12.
- [DeepThink: A Conceptual Model for Knowledge-Addressable Recurrent Language Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.16171): DeepThink is a conceptual framework, without experiments, for recurrent language models: at each step a Knowledge Activator picks Knowledge Bank units to assemble a Shared Thinking Operator; for compatible templates, an existing fixed-depth model can be realized exactly under a fixed schedule. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-10-12.
- [Running Fewer Loops Removes Refusal Behaviour in Recurrent-Depth Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.15218): At half its trained depth Ouro-1.4B-Thinking keeps 89% of its GSM8K accuracy, but its harmful-request help rate rises from 0.038 to 0.205 although a linear classifier still detects harm after one loop (ROC AUC 0.967); training at random depths keeps Huginn-0125 at or below 0.040 from 1 to 32 loops. Category: safety; focus: core; 2026-10-10.
- [Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14998): Tab-Loop replaces the 12 untied in-context-learning blocks of the tabular foundation model TabICLv2 with 4 tied blocks applied k times; at matched pretraining and inference compute it matches the untied baseline with 62% fewer parameters (10.4M vs. 27.6M), and accuracy rises with the number of loops. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-10.
- [Learning to Extrapolate in Depth with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14456): For looped Transformers on all-pairs graph connectivity, proves that training at depth K converges to an update rule with one effective parameter, giving a finite extrapolation window with explicit endpoints; a test depth chosen from the training distribution alone can guarantee recovery on much harder graphs. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-10-10.
- [Adaptive-Depth Is a Finishing Stage](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14252): Fixed-first training keeps a looped Transformer at one depth and varies depth only in a short final phase; at 200M, depth 2 for the first 67% of the run cuts modeled compute by 45% with mean NLL across inference depths within 0.5% of all-depth training, and at 1B it saves 31% to 37% with final NLL within 0.8%. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-09.
- [Scaling RNA Foundation Models through Iterative Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13106): Eco-RNA, an 80M-parameter RNA foundation model, repeats a shared input-conditioned Transformer core between a prelude and coda, trained at sampled depths; four iterations instead of one raise RNAGym aggregate absolute Spearman from 0.242 to 0.286 and beat Evo 2 40B on all three aggregate fitness metrics. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-09.
- [RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13041): RAMP runs the first 24 of Huginn-0125's 32 recurrent steps with FP8 weight-and-activation computation and the last 8 in BF16, as earlier quantization error is attenuated by later steps; up to 4K context it keeps near-full-precision prefill quality with up to 1.16× first-prefill speedup on an NVIDIA H100. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-09.
- [One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12582): ELR trains looped LMs without the one-loop tax using a gated state update, loop counts mixed within each optimizer update and loop-index and budget conditioning; on 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrids, one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 above the matched baseline (ten-task average), and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-08.
- [One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12448): reViT reuses one Transformer block across a vision encoder's depth, with each depth's FFN a convex combination of shared experts programmed by normalized depth; trained from scratch, reViT-B/16 attains DeiT III accuracy with about 70% fewer stored parameters, and one checkpoint runs at multiple depths. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-08.
- [Scaling to Tens of Thousands of Test-Time Iterations with Loop-Native Attention Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11570): InfiLoop swaps the carry-last state update of looped reasoners for a loop-native residual that weights past states by content and learned decay in constant memory; a 7M-parameter model reaches 97.9% exact accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme and 13.6% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-2, improving beyond 20,000 effective steps. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-08.
- [From Chain-of-Thought to Loops: Non-Autoregressive Latent Reasoning via Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11472): LLoCoT loops the full Qwen3-1.7B-Base backbone over a fixed workspace of latent slots, then samples all latent thoughts in parallel to condition answer decoding; on HumanEval and MBPP it matches explicit-CoT Reasoning SFT while cutting time to the first answer token by approximately 36×. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-08.
- [Invariant-Measure Reasoners: Stable Representations for Latent Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10996): ImR predicts from the prediction head's output averaged along a recurrent block's latent trajectory, approximating its invariant measure, rather than from the final state; head-only fine-tuning and from-scratch training reduce prediction instability and improve accuracy in many maze and Sudoku settings. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-07.
- [Safe at One Loop, Risky at Another: Aligning Safety Across Recurrent Depths in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10625): Jailbreaks on Ouro LoopLMs can succeed more at deeper recurrent depths and transfer across depths; SafeBridge adds depth-specific control of shared layers, selective state bridging and joint cross-depth safety supervision, cutting matched- and cross-depth attack success while improving general utility. Category: safety; focus: core; 2026-10-07.
- [Recurrent Self-Improvement: Dynamic Cross-Loop On-Policy Distillation for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10623): LoopOPD post-trains a looped LM by distilling its frozen terminal-loop policy into an intermediate-loop student on the student's own rollouts, and D-LoopOPD refreshes that teacher as the shared weights update; on Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, D-LoopOPD raises terminal-loop AIME 2024 Avg@16 from 62.08 to 71.67. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-07.
- [Executing Causal Structure Learning with Linear-Attention Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10395): Builds a fixed-weight linear-attention Transformer block that exactly performs one update of an acyclicity-constrained continuous causal-discovery method, so repeated blocks reproduce its trajectory; the multiplier must be carried between updates, and trained attention models do not reliably execute it. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-10-07.
- [ResidualQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers with 2-Bit Residuals](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10381): ResidualQuant keeps a looped Transformer's final-loop KV as reference and stores other loops as low-precision residuals, with least-square scaling, rotation and loop-wise mixed precision; it stays close to BF16 accuracy, cuts theoretical KV storage by 80.7% and improves peak throughput by up to 5.38x. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-07.
- [Input-Blind Controls Produce Substantial Oracle Headroom for Layer Programs in Multiple-Choice Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10368): For 32 layer-skipping and repetition programs on Qwen3-4B-Base and Llama-3.1-8B, input-blind controls give 10.2-11.8 and 15.6-19.4 percentage points of oracle headroom with shared option order, above the real programs' 9.0 and 10.1, so headroom does not establish a layer-specific benefit. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-10-07.
- [Enabling Dynamic Computation in Looped LMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09013): Ragged KV, a best-available KV cache, lets early-exiting tokens in Ouro-style looped LMs stop computing by aliasing deeper KV entries to their exit-depth cache, cutting FLOPs and KV memory by up to 30% at full-depth performance; a corrected early-exit prior makes tokens exit at heterogeneous depths. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-06.
- [Hybrid Latent Attention for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07940): HLA keeps exact KV only for a window of recent tokens and stores older ones as compact latents that each loop's query reads directly; uptrained on frozen Ouro looped models (T=4), it cuts the cache 10.7x per token, speeds decoding up to 7.4x at 16K and retains over 97% of the original accuracy on math, knowledge and reasoning. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-06.
- [SanSi: A Looped Typed Decision Model for System 1.5 Thinking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07730): SanSi turns the pretrained looped LM Ouro into a typed decision model that reads option probabilities after every loop, each trained with a proper scoring rule; on 10,027 test decisions it reaches 72.0% accuracy, 13.5 points above a non-looped model of the same shape trained with the same recipe. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-06.
- [Recurrent Looped Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07591): RLT splits its layers into a parallel causal encoder and a recurrent decoder fed the previous token's final decoder state; trained on at most 40 bits, two splits reach 100% parity accuracy at 256 bits, and on swap-based S_5 at eight times the training length it reaches 97% versus under 1% for a Transformer. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-10-06.
- [TAFFY: A Task-Adaptive Tabular Foundation Model with In-Context Diversity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07559): TAFFY, a tabular foundation model, loops a shared ICL Transformer stack over contextual representations with a task-conditioned gate on the final update, and pretrains on contexts mixing causally related environments; it attains the lowest average rank across six classification and five regression benchmark datasets. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-06.
- [Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06833): Shows that near fixed points looped LMs can skip recurrence paths in training, decoding, prefill and RL; its learned depth prior and orthogonal input injection lower perplexity over existing choices from 100M to 1.6B. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-10-05.
- [LiFT: Loop Flow Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05538): LiFT loops a shared DiT core and trains each step toward a point on a straight path from the initial estimate to the flow-matching target, indexed by continuous depth, so it can loop past training depth; on ImageNet 256x256, LiFT-L/2 beats DiT-XL/2 by 3.34 FID with approximately 60% fewer parameters. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-04.
- [Loopy: Low-Bit Quantization Framework for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05265): Loopy quantizes the shared core of looped LMs after training, picking channel-scaling and rotation configurations by final prediction loss at the target deployment depth, with calibration windows going to promising candidates; on Ouro-1.4B under W4A4 it cuts LAMBADA perplexity by 36.5% versus SpinQuant. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-04.
- [LoopMoEVR: Loop-Based Degradation-Aware Mixture-of-Experts for Unified UHD Video Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05109): LoopMoEVR loops two parameter-shared MoE layers between a video encoder and decoder, conditioned on degradation and video state, with a depth predictor setting the loop count; with approximately 0.884M parameters, one model handles four UHD video restoration tasks with the highest mean PSNR on UHV-4K-AIO. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-04.
- [AdaLoop: Adaptive-Depth Latent Reasoning for Audio Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06949): AdaLoop replaces the encoder-to-LM connector of audio LMs with a shared Transformer block that iterates over audio features, guided by the question, until a learned halting unit stops it; with fewer than 3% extra parameters it raises average accuracy by 2.9 to 3.8 points on MMSU, MMAU-Pro and MMAR. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-03.
