- [Dynamic Routing as a New Dimension for Test-time Versatility of LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04751): Training-free dynamic routing fits programs that skip layers or repeat blocks of a frozen LLM's layers from 3 or 10 demonstrations, with the model's confidence arbitrating; it gains on average over MMLU's 49 tasks, doubles a 7B model's ARC-AGI accuracy where its CoT fails, and complements CoT. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-10-03.
- [ALoDLM: Adaptively Looped Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04198): ALoDLM converts Qwen3 into a diffusion language model whose recurrent core gives unresolved tokens extra passes while confident tokens commit as context, with exit schedules learned through a NELBO; at 1.7B and 8B it beats all evaluated DLMs and the AR baselines in average score on eleven benchmarks. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-10-03.
- [On the Chain-of-Thought Monitorability of Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02741): Across eight MonitorBench tasks, raising Ouro-1.4B-Thinking's loop depth from T=4 to T=8 lowers stress-test CoT monitorability on some tasks (Logic 77.9% to 41.8% under Direct Concealment), but looped LMs are not systematically less monitorable than non-looped LMs matched on size or depth. Category: safety; focus: core; 2026-10-02.
- [The Surprising Effectiveness of Shared Memory in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02383): LPT pretrains looped LMs where only the first recursion writes a KV cache and later recursions read it plus a short local window; at 150M-1B parameters with five recursions, the hybrid variant cuts FineWeb-Edu validation perplexity by 1.12-1.82 versus a same-size standard Transformer with 76-79% less context memory. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-01.
- [Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02185): LoopCD, a training-free contrastive decoder, contrasts a looped Transformer's final prediction with an earlier recurrent pass; it lifts Ouro-2.6B-Thinking's AIME 2024 pass@1 from 61.88% to 73.33%, and at half the loops matches or exceeds full-depth unguided baselines while cutting forward FLOPs by 22.5% to 48.2%. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-10-01.
- [Universal interpolation for deep residual self-attention networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01981): Proves universal interpolation for deep residual softmax attention under strong parameter reuse: two frozen single-head blocks with Gaussian-initialized projections, with only their order, signs and durations chosen per task, map any N sequences of n tokens to any other N, at continuous and finite depth. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-10-01.
- [LAST: Looped Audio Spectrogram Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01926): LAST runs six shared blocks over all audio tokens once, then reuses them to refine only the class token against cached audio keys and values; on AudioSet ten-pass LAST reaches 0.345 mAP, 2.1% relative above a twelve-layer sequential transformer, with 49.4% fewer parameters and 42% fewer MACs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-10-01.
- [Looping Beyond Twice: A Scalable Recipe for Looped Mixture-of-Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01153): LOOM loops a whole MoE decoder with residual scaling, input-embedding re-injection every loop, per-loop routers over shared experts and a Looping Residual; under near-iso-FLOP the 700M model performs best at 5 loops, cutting perplexity from 18.36 to 16.54 over the non-looped baseline. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-10-01.
- [Rotate the Loop: Blockwise Conformality for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14030): Blockwise conformal injections make the map applied to the residual between loop steps rotate coordinate-aligned groups, each at its own rate; on A5 word problems, last-token accuracy at T=32 rises from 0.692 with Parcae's diagonal map to 0.894, and FineWeb perplexity and LAMBADA also improve. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-30.
- [Closing the Loop: Practical Training Recipes for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00673): Closing the Loop trains a 1.4B looped LM from scratch on 310B tokens instead of Ouro's 7.7T, beating a parameter-matched dense model on all 12 benchmarks (+14 points on GSM8K, +10 on MATH, +22 on DROP), and converts Qwen3-1.7B-Base into Looped Qwen with one learned input-mixing scalar and a smoothed exit loss. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-09-30.
- [Random Recursive Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.00541): RRM keeps a pool of L learned layers and, at each of T recursive steps, samples one layer with replacement per example; on reasoning tasks including Sudoku, Maze-Hard and ARC-AGI-1 it matches or exceeds baselines, often with 50-75% fewer parameters, and can run deeper at inference than in training. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-30.
- [Scaling Laws for Looped Mixture of Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40316): Loop Scaling Laws jointly model recurrence, MoE sparsity, model size and data; looping the middle block gives ~2x total-parameter efficiency on reasoning and sparsity ~3x active-parameter efficiency, and at trillion-token scale a looped MoE matches a ~2x larger non-looped MoE on reasoning at matched compute. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-09-30.
- [Looped Diffusion Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.40305): Looped-DiT repeats shared middle Transformer blocks within each denoising step of a text-to-image diffusion Transformer, adding deep supervision across loops and self-modulating attention; a 260M-parameter looped model surpasses a model 6.5x larger on multiple benchmarks with 4.9x lower inference compute. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-30.
- [What Limits Recursive Reasoning Models: Optimization, Architecture and Test-Time Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39967): Ablations of HRM-, TRM- and URM-style recursive reasoners show that stable training needs an intermediate gradient horizon, large physical batches and controlled state updates, not explicit hierarchy; its 13.6M-parameter model lifts Arithmetic OOD accuracy to 71.2% from 36.2% and reaches 98.41% on Sudoku. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-30.
- [Shared Weights, Selected Computations: How Looped Transformers Route What Each Loop Does](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39892): In looped Transformers trained on graph walks, each loop need not perform the same step: predictions advance by varying numbers of graph steps, and a learned linear map J on the entering hidden state steers a frozen loop to different transitions, which activation patching traces to attention routing. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-30.
- [A Tilted Bowl Is Not a Slippery Slope: Compressing Looped Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.39277): In more than 30 compressed looped models from five families, fixed rounding error only shifts where a settling loop comes to rest; stopping at the halting head, then finishing with 8-bit loops, beats fixed depth by up to 15 points on Sudoku-Extreme and Maze-Hard under a third of the weight traffic. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-30.
- [LoopVL: Recurrent Visual Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38426): LoopVL-1B runs a joint vision-language state through two shared 16-layer stacks in an [L×3→H]×2 schedule (128 layer calls); trained from scratch on 0.14T tokens, it outperforms a range of similarly sized and larger non-recurrent models on multimodal understanding and visual reasoning benchmarks. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [Pretraining Latent Information Feedback Transformers with Teacher Supervision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38149): LIFT feeds each position's predicted state, a next-token distribution, back as input at the next position and trains in parallel on states precomputed by a pretrained teacher LM; from 135M to 1B parameters it beats standard Transformers at matched tokens and is on par with or ahead of compute-matched ones. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [Thinking in Depth, Speaking Directly: Recurrent Latent Reasoning for Paralinguistically Grounded Spoken Dialogue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37818): LoopSLM loops layers L9–11 of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B four times, re-anchoring each pass to acoustic memory, with two-stage CoT-to-response training; against the CoT-SFT baseline it gains over 20 points in reasoning accuracy while generating 64.5% fewer tokens at half the latency. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [Looped Actor: Depth-Recurrent Reasoning Models for Reinforcement Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37432): Looped Actor, an RL policy, applies a shared Transformer block toward a fixed point and halts once its action distribution stabilizes; on 22 tasks in six environments it matches or beats an untied baseline with 16× more parameters, and on Boxoban its loop count grows with the pushes left. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-29.
- [Looped Transformers as Optimizers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37379): Viewing the looped hidden state as a fast weight updated by local gradient steps, the paper derives loop transitions from a projection, objective and optimizer rule; its OperLoop beats the compared looped and non-looped baselines in average generative performance at matched training FLOPs. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [Scheduling Recursive Reasoning in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36653): TAPS adapts the scale of each recurrent update online from the balance of persistent progress and fluctuation, instead of a fixed unit scale; training-free, it improves TRM on Sudoku and Maze and Ouro and Huginn on language benchmarks, and with training it reaches up to 1.56 times wall-clock speedup at matched accuracy. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [What Makes Recurrence Effective in Looped Language Models?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36636): Pretrains looped LMs with a fixed loop count and tests them below, at and beyond it: extra loops help reasoning but hurt knowledge, non-recurrent output layers add robustness to under-unrolling, and channel-wise history-state injection with timestep conditioning better preserves knowledge under extended unrolling. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36585): Thirteen base models reliably follow only 1.4-3.6 lines of in-context references and extra pretrained loops add little; a rank-8 LoRA at one early layer, weights frozen, lifts Qwen3-8B from 15.5% to 99% on 24-line chains and lets Ouro-1.4B reach 60 lines after four loops and at least 160 after eight. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-29.
- [LoopICL: Looping a single transformer block to solve tabular tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36108): LoopICL loops a single Transformer block with coupled cell and row streams for tabular in-context learning, varying loop counts in pre-training and exiting with a learned gate; at the same FLOPs it performs competitively with TabICLv2 on TabArena and TALENT while using nearly 90% fewer parameters. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-28.
- [How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35751): Foil loops an MoE core whose experts and routers are shared across passes while each pass gets its own attention, and flattens it into fewer, wider layers with more passes at fixed expert parameters and compute; at 100B tokens the most flattened Foil ends 0.012 nat below the unflattened looped baseline. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-09-28.
- [Improving Test-Time Scaling with Adaptive Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35748): TaH2 post-trains a looped Qwen3 backbone jointly with a token-level iteration decider supervised by online lookahead depth labels, so only tokens that benefit get extra iterations; on AIME it raises the accuracy-compute slope by 53% (2.74 vs. 1.79) over the non-looped baseline. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-09-28.
- [Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34538): DAS lets shallow-depth drafts in looped Transformers read full-depth values of the verified prefix (Mature-V) at no extra recurrent cost; DAS-Wave adds parallel refinement, progressive block growth and a full-depth verifier, reaching 4.00-6.96× mean throughput speedup over full-depth autoregressive decoding. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-28.
- [FlexLoop: Depth-Elastic Looped Policies for Adaptive Test-Time Computation in Deep RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34488): FlexLoop post-trains fixed-depth looped RL policies with the RL objective plus adjacent-depth policy distillation so shallower depths become reliable; on 30 long-horizon goal-conditioned environments it keeps full-depth performance, cuts average recurrent depth by up to 43% and gives up to 1.34× speedup in a stress test. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-28.
- [Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34218): Loop Dropout randomly masks a shared LoRA adapter's application at individual loops of a looped LM and rescales kept applications by inverse survival probability; fine-tuning Ouro-1.4B on math, it raises MATH-500 accuracy from 38.87% with LoRA to 47.53%, keeping standard LoRA inference. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-09-28.
- [MoR-MLLM: Mixture of Recursions for Efficient Multimodal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08830): MoR-MLLM brings Mixture-of-Recursions to multimodal LLMs, giving each token an adaptive recursion depth, trained with a three-stage MoR-Tuning strategy and an entropy-regularized routing loss; versus recent tiny MLLMs it cuts training memory and computation while keeping vision-language performance. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-09-27.
- [Reasoning on the Simplex: Geometric Fixed-Point Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33540): GFPR iterates a weight-tied map on categorical beliefs over a product of simplices, whose argmax is the answer at every step; at about 7M parameters it reaches 95.1% on Sudoku-Extreme and 92.0% on Maze-Hard, and a 201M language model with 24 Picard steps beats GPT-2 small on four zero-shot tasks. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-27.
- [Beyond the Training Horizon: Mechanisms and Limits of Length Generalization in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33144): Compares two looped Transformers: MR-Loop updates an intermediate state at a fixed readout, DR-Loop propagates intermediate states along an advancing frontier; both degrade at greater depths, and live-consumed and fresh-aged residual directions causally control computation beyond the training horizon. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-27.
- [Write Back the $Δ$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.32457): ReFlux trains a sparse router over a frozen Transformer that writes depth increments Δ back to earlier layers, in a second traversal of the same token or streamed to the next token; it lowers perplexity on ten corpora and raises accuracy by 2.1-2.3 points, reaching 4.7 on multi-hop reasoning. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-26.
- [Programs-of-Layers in LLMs through the Lens of Cortical Areas](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31360): Reproducing PoLar's skip-or-repeat layer programs for frozen LLMs with MCTS on 6 models, repeating beats skipping and both together beat either, but with a format-fixing prompt the router's top prediction collapses to the standard pass, though its top-5 programs still gain. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-25.
- [Quantizing Looped Transformers: Feedback Exposure and Calibration Blindness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.30820): In post-training quantization of looped Transformers, per-channel INT4 on Huginn-3.5B fails mainly at the non-residual loop-entry adapter and one-step GPTQ is worse than RTN on five of nine checkpoints; accumulating GPTQ's Hessian across recurrence steps beats both on all nine and recovers bf16-level accuracy on Huginn. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-25.
- [FlashLoop: Fast and Memory-Efficient Looped Transformers via Lazy Updates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29812): FlashLoop, a training-free inference framework, cuts cross-loop redundancy in looped Transformers with token-sparse updates, sparse attention and KV-residual quantization, giving up to 1.64x speedup and 6x less KV-cache memory while largely preserving accuracy. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-24.
- [Depth through recurrence: Looped transformers for flow-matching TTS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29768): Compares seven weight-reuse layouts with 18 block calls in flow-matching TTS; SEQUENCE, running each of nine blocks twice in a row, stays competitive at 32 steps with 47.1% fewer parameters, while at four steps Suffix's word error rate exceeds Prefix's by 3.44 and 5.97 percentage points on the two datasets. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-24.
- [FluidRain: Incompressible Rain Flow as an Attention Bias for Loop-in-Loop Video Deraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.29006): FluidRain reuses one rain-flow-guided block stack across three scales, each output becoming the next scale's state, and one attention operator across three frames (Loop-in-Loop); the 0.80M-parameter video derainer stays competitive with substantially larger restoration models on four benchmarks. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-24.
- [Stream Recursion Model (SRM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28809): SRM, an HRM variant built for interpretability, recursively refines multiple latent streams with a weight-tied layer function and learned stream-wise attention; on OpenWebText SRM-base reaches training loss 3.18 with 68M parameters at 7 times the compute time, versus 3.20 for a 124M GPT-2. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-23.
- [Attention Routing Stabilizes Early: Working-Set Inference for Recurrent Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27373): WISE, training-free, uses full attention in early recurrent steps of a recurrent-depth LM to find a block-sparse working set and reuses that support later; it largely preserves full-attention multi-hop QA performance, with up to a 1.76x late-step attention speedup over native FlashAttention at 4K context. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-23.
- [When Recursive Models Finish Computing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26487): Extending attention- and MLP-based Tiny Recursive Models from their nominal 16 steps to 512 raises cumulative exact-solve accuracy on 1,000 hard Sudoku puzzles from 59.2% to 87.5% and from 74.4% to 91.9%; completed states are locally contractive along the trajectory while their Jacobians keep strongly expanding directions. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-22.
- [Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.25778): Looping one shared block lets residual feedforward networks and post-LN Transformers attain the minimax polynomial rate for Hölder targets up to logarithmic factors with a fixed number of bounded parameters, while at large fixed budgets the best untied family's worst-case risk stays bounded away from zero. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-09-22.
- [LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24196): LoopCD contrasts the logits of an earlier loop iteration with those of the final iteration when decoding from looped LMs, refining uncertain hard tokens without training; it improves Huginn-0125 and Ouro-1.4B on arithmetic reasoning, code generation and question answering with negligible overhead. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-21.
- [WaveFront Decoding: Parallelized Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.23033): Wavefront Decoding is a training-free self-speculative decoder for looped language models that co-batches shallow drafting and full-depth verification in the same recurrent-block calls, reaching 2.42x speedup on Ouro-2.6B and 3.54x on Huginn-3.5B over autoregressive decoding. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-19.
- [Trading Depth for Time in Recurrent Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21605): Adds a latent thought token after each vocabulary token of a Latent Recurrent Transformer, refining the state again through the shared backbone; at matched training FLOPs it beats PonderLM-2, overtakes a two-loop Transformer as compute grows, and recovers on average 89% of the gains of doubling LRT depth. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-09-18.
- [Prediction Dynamics in Depth-Recurrent Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.21383): Analyzing how Huginn-3.5B and Ouro-1.4B change answer scores across recurrent depth, the paper derives a sharp margin characterization; accounting for update direction and competitor pairing reduces the mean earliest qualifying depth by a further 22.5-34.4% of the total depth beyond translation removal. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-18.
- [Beyond Depth Truncation: Controlled Evaluation of Depth Utilization in Recursive Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19934): The Depth Control Protocol decomposes depth-truncation curves of depth-recurrent LMs; on the 542.8M Sona model the 1.4251 nat naive depth effect splits into 47.9% block applications, -2.8% distinct depth and 54.8% inter-block composition, and sampled-depth training removes the calibration confounder. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-17.
- [CoReLoop: Parameter-Efficient Controlled Recurrent Refinement for Audio Deepfake Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19818): CoReLoop loops a frozen SSL audio deepfake detector's encoder on its own output, adding loop-specific LoRA and light modules that adapt recurrent inputs, regulate state updates and align outputs; on the 24-layer model two passes cut pooled EER from 4.85% to 3.74% while training about 11M of 598M parameters. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-17.
- [Storing Is Not Remembering: LSTM-UT and Bounded Gated Memory for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19521): On Rule 30, a state-only Block Universal Transformer (BUT) extrapolates and recalls better than CoTFormer, which caches every step's KV; LSTM-UT adds a small bounded gated cell state to the shared block, keeps 99.7% exact-row accuracy at depth 60 after training to depth 12, and beats BUT on OpenWebText2. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-09-17.
- [How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107): In prelude-core-coda looped Transformers, growing the number of core passes during training, with or without shared weights, and a normalize-and-inject boundary operator raise pre-training scaling exponents; a 7.4B untied growth model matches GPT-3 13B on CORE with roughly 20× less compute. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-09-16.
- [MoRE: Mixture of Reused Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.18176): MoRE shares MoE expert pools across groups of adjacent layers, keeping per-layer routers and a learnable depth embedding before routing; at 114M-1.15B parameters it gets lower perplexity and stronger downstream results than standard MoEs and weight-sharing architectures at matched compute and parameters. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-09-16.
- [LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184): LoopSpec, a training-free self-speculative decoder for looped Transformers, drafts tokens from early recurrent states and overlaps drafting with verification; it stays lossless under greedy and sampling decoding and reaches up to 6.83× speedup. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-09-15.
- [Right Direction, Wrong Step: Geometric Analysis of Finite-Step Failure in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16665): Analyzing Ouro-1.4B, Ouro-2.6B and Huginn-0125, the paper finds that harmful extra loop iterations often move in a locally helpful direction but take too large a step; a fixed quarter step recovers positive reference utility for 72.2–83.2% of selected failures across four settings. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-15.
- [T-LoopFormer: Token-Level Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers with Dynamic Routing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15160): T-LoopFormer's router gives each token its own number of loops through a shared block based on its initial hidden state, and a recursion-wise KV cache keeps per-loop entries only for active tokens; it decodes 2.24× faster than LoopFormer and has the lowest decoding latency among baselines. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-09-14.
- [Temporal Recurrence Favors Fewer Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.12531): Sweeps within-step depth, expert width and expert count at matched per-step compute for models that carry latent state across steps (the Transformer feeds its final residual stream into the first layer at the next token); on Sokoban and FineWeb, recurrence shifts the best observed allocation toward substantially fewer layers. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-09-11.
- [Thinking with Looped Flows](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11801): Trains looped models with local denoising objectives at decreasing noise levels and infers by integrating a probability flow; across six reasoning benchmarks it outperforms prior looped models overall, reaching 58.8% test accuracy on ARC-AGI-1. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-10.
- [LoopVAE: Recurrent Depth Across Scales for Visual Tokenization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11516): LoopVAE reuses one scale- and loop-conditioned four-block core across all scales and loops of a visual tokenizer's encoder and decoder (28 block applications each); on ImageNet-256 the 29M-parameter CNN reaches 0.28 rFID and 32.54 dB PSNR with approximately 65% fewer parameters than 84M reference VAEs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-10.
- [Looped GPT-BERT: Trading Parameters for Computation in Small Language Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09691): Looped GPT-BERT runs four physical layers for twelve traversals with GPT-BERT's MNTP and CLM objectives in BabyLM 2026 Strict-small; the 12.18M-parameter 4×12 model scores 71.19 on BLiMP, near GPT-BERT causal-focus at 71.66 and above GPT-2 at 65.23, but trails both on GLUE. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-09-09.
- [RecurTrace: Adaptive Latent Reasoning with Loop-Time Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03379): Loops a middle block of an LM, adding attention over earlier loop states and an oracle-supervised halting head; on MathQA it reaches 56.9% with 2.0 loops on average, 2.2 points above the best fixed depth. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-09-03.
- [Looped Transformers under the Jacobian Lens: Does the Global Workspace Survive Recurrence?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01924): Applies an extended Jacobian lens to Ouro-2.6B and Huginn-0125: both form a workspace in their iterated part, but Ouro rebuilds content every loop, while Huginn carries it forward and interventions act within about two recurrences. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-09-01.
- [Diffusion as a Training Curriculum for Timestep-Free Iterative Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01449): A timestep-free diffusion denoiser with a persistent hidden state, built from a looped block reused at every step, becomes an anytime solver that improves with inference depth, reaching 99.90% exact solve on Sudoku-Extreme and 98.93% on Maze-Unique; annealed corruption matters mainly as a training curriculum. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-09-01.
- [Latent Recurrent Thoughts: Recurrent Refinement of Proposed Latents for Reasoning with Frozen LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01117): LRT feeds a frozen Qwen3-8B decoder latents that a task-dedicated proposer drafts and a tiny TRM-style recurrent reasoner refines over many steps; it beats prior frozen-decoder continuous-space reasoning methods and, at a small fraction of its inference compute, non-thinking-mode CoT prompting. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-09-01.
- [Universal Transformers for Circuit Computations: Perfect Length Generalization in Tiny Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.31067): A provably correct Universal Transformer (280 learnable parameters for Boolean algebra) cuts circuit depth by one per iteration via a depth-tracking positional encoding and halts after d iterations on depth-d inputs; trained on depths 1 and 2, it reaches 100% accuracy on deeper Boolean, modular arithmetic and ListOps problems. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-08-31.
- [Evaluating Tiny Recursive Models Across Training for Code Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29376): Compares a ~28M-parameter autoregressive Tiny Recursive Model (TRM-AR) that reuses one two-layer block with parameter- and depth-matched Transformers on Python code generation; it beats the parameter-matched control at roughly 175 times its per-step cost, but the depth-matched model fits and generates better. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-08-29.
- [Training-Free Hidden-State Refinement for Flow-Matching Image Generators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.29160): A training-free method repeats selected transformer layers inside each denoising call of frozen flow-matching image generators, controlling token scope, sampling-progress gating and Loop Guidance; on Scale-RAE DiT2.4B, Loop Guidance raises GenEval from 0.4471 to 0.5691 and DPG-Bench from 0.7656 to 0.8053. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-29.
- [Squeezing More from Limited Data with Recursive Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26973): RecursiveGPT applies one shared Transformer block R times with step-specific norms and factorized embeddings; in BabyLM-scale pretraining the 404.1M RecursiveGPT-Large averages 63.93 at 100M words versus 63.47 for a 1.22B standard Transformer, and a 27.6M model wins all three evaluations at 10M words. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-08-27.
- [Dynamical phase selection controls compute scaling in looped transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26556): Looped transformers that iterate one weight-tied attention-plus-MLP block and reach identical accuracy realize distinct dynamical phases depending on initialization; the fold phase gives the workload tail P(τ>N) ∼ N^-2, while in the Neimark-Sacker phase this fold scaling law disappears. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-08-27.
- [Can a Dynamic Internal Field Govern a Transformer's Cognition? Certifiability, not Superiority, in Homeostatic Compute Control](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24319): A homeostatic field (PDEs on the module graph) modulates the halting threshold and block gain of a PonderNet-style looped reasoner in 4.2–5.6M-parameter Transformers on S5 state tracking; wave, diffusion, gated and Navier-Stokes physics tie on accuracy, and its edge is an exact runtime stability check. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-08-25.
- [Steering Recurrent Reasoners at Inference Time with Readout Feedback](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24136): Readout Feedback (RoFB) feeds a recurrent reasoner's intermediate readout probabilities back into its latent dynamics as token-wise pairwise coupling forces at test time; on Sudoku and Maze with AKOrN, ItrSA++ and TRM it clearly helps four of six model-task pairs, beyond what more steps or trajectories reach. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-25.
- [TANGO: Treating Tokens as Operators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22117): TANGO merges attention and FFN in a looped model's shared block into one operator where attention-averaged source-token gates scale destination features; at matched parameters and data it has the lowest mean test NLL in all 16 settings, and its development loss never rises from depth 4 to 8 to 16. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-08-22.
- [Allocating Recurrent Compute in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18230): MixerLoop repeats each Gated DeltaNet mixer while applying the dense FFN once per layer; it surpasses full-block recurrence on aggregate CORE at 15M and keeps 41.5% of full-block recurrence's CORE improvement at 110M while cutting recurrent-backbone projection FLOPs by 45.9%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-08-18.
- [Think Shallow, Solve Deep: Controlling Recurrent Dynamics for Reliable Test-Time Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18222): Shows that a trained recurrent operator's dynamical regime (settling, marginal or drifting) predicts whether extra test-time iterations help, preserve or degrade answers on algorithmic tasks; a terminal fixed-point objective controls the regime. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-18.
- [Recirculation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.17981): Recirculation feeds part of a deep layer activation into a shallow layer of frozen pretrained transformers, adding recurrence over depth and tokens; adaptive recirculation on Gemma3 lowers perplexity and raises relative GSM8k accuracy by 21%. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-08-18.
- [Looped Language Models Improve Compositional Tool Calling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.18171): Evaluates native (Ouro) and retrofitted (Llama-3.2-1B, OLMo-2-1B) looped LMs on API-Bank, BFCL and NESTful with matched fine-tuning; looping mainly helps compositional, dependency-aware tool calls, multi-step accuracy generally rises with depth, and adaptive inference gives a better compute-performance trade-off. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-08-17.
- [Gated Recurrent Transformers: Expressive Depth through Recurrent Modulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15062): Gated Recurrent Transformer iterates a shared core between prelude and coda blocks, gating each update on the hidden state, prelude output and noise; a 3-layer model matches 12-layer GPT-2 Small at similar FLOPs, and at large scale it cuts parameters by 63% and peak decoding memory by 59% for 10% more latency. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-08-15.
- [Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14290): Mobius-v0 shares one global FFN memory across all layers, queried repeatedly by self-attention reasoners via hidden states; a 7B model trained from scratch matches a 7B Transformer with 62.6% of its training data, and Intern-S2-Mobius (from Qwen3.5-35B) gives nearly 4x end-to-end inference speedup. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-08-14.
- [Nanbeige4.2-3B on Apple Silicon: Fixing Deployment Bugs and Decreasing Looped Transformer Memory Overhead](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13987): Fixes five bugs that stop the Nanbeige4.2-3B looped Transformer (one layer stack run twice) from running on Apple Silicon, and adds chunked prefill against its doubled peak attention memory, extending allowable context width by 2.7× on 32 GiB; the patched model completes up to 30% of MCPMark-subset tasks. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-08-14.
- [Mimir: A Sub-2B Hierarchical Reasoning Model Trained on Permissible Data Punches Above Its Weight Class](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13517): Mimir is a 1.78B HRM-Text model whose low- and high-level stacks are applied repeatedly in an interleaved schedule, trained from scratch on 161 permissible datasets; across 20 benchmarks Mimir v1.5 has the best average of all sub-2B models in every domain, beating HRM-Text 1B, Ouro 1.4B and Ouro 2.6B. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-08-13.
- [MergeOver: Post-Training Token Merging for Recursive Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13141): MergeOver adds Token Merging to the weight-shared Sliced Recursive Transformer without retraining, merging at each stage's first block and keeping length fixed across its recursions; on ImageNet-1K top-1 drops 1.47 percentage points while GPU peak activation memory falls 37.3% and 38.4% at batch sizes 1 and 16. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-13.
- [BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09888): BDH-CQ writes ARC demonstrations into a recurrent memory, then solves the query by iterating one latent update before decoding; a 150M-parameter configuration reaches 29.5% pass@2 on the public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set at a computed inference cost of $0.0007 per task. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-10.
- [Depth-adaptive Inference of Looped Language Models via Continuous Depth Batching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09444): Continuous depth batching forms new batches between loop steps so looped LMs can serve tokens exiting at different depths; on Ouro 1.4B and Huginn 3.5B it realizes up to 99% of the estimated maximum speedup. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-08-10.
- [Full-bandwidth transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08888): Fuses each step's top-layer state with the sampled token embedding through a gate and feeds it back as the next input; 1B models match or approach standard transformers trained on roughly 1.5x more tokens. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-08-09.
- [Think Deep, Speak Once: Relit, A Recursive Latent Implicit Transformer Framework](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08113): ReLIT places a trainable recursive Transformer block with learned halting between a frozen TinyLlama-1.1B backbone and its frozen LM head, refining a latent state over iterations; training only this block, it reaches 98.60% accuracy on ProofWriter and 97.60% on RuleTaker. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-08-08.
- [bioMoR: Biology-Guided Mixture-of-Recursions for Effective Genomic Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06727): bioMoR applies Mixture-of-Recursions to omics data, adding biological-graph knowledge to embeddings, attention and the router that sets each gene or pathway token's recursion depth; across eight benchmarks it raises average macro-F1 by 8.2 percentage points over the best biology-agnostic MoR baseline. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-07.
- [Iterate or Widen? When Test-Time Refinement Helps LiDAR Scene Completion: A Controlled Study of Evidence Geometry, Training Coverage, and Compute](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06014): For LiDAR scene completion, a 0.53M-parameter weight-tied multigrid refiner iterated on a frozen one-shot predictor beats a parameter-matched wider predictor by 0.911 mIoU points under contiguous angular removal, but adds only 0.300 under 75% thinning, where observation-family augmentation adds 5.975. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-06.
- [MACRO: Markov Chain Routing of Transformer Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05872): MACRO learns a task-specific Markov policy over skip, repeat and hidden-state-addition moves through a frozen LLM's layers, decoded with top-k Viterbi; it gains +5.0% average accuracy over unrouted baselines and +7.2% over Dr. LLM while cutting route-search time 9.4x (from 14.8 to 1.6 hours). Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-08-06.
- [LoopMTP: A looped transformer guided by latent multi-token prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03624): LoopMTP loops the whole Transformer stack, softly aligning the hidden state of loop t with the embedding of the token t steps ahead and gating information across iterations; it improves average accuracy by up to 8.1% (relative) over the non-looped baseline, with training stable for up to 15 loops. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-08-04.
- [The Ignition Is Real, and It Lives at the Readout: Latent composition, difficulty-clocked ignition, and the interface-constituted commit in a recurrent-depth reasoner](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03263): Regrowing a published 30M-parameter recurrent-depth reasoner shows its compositional ignition is real and sits at the readout: arrival time rises with problem depth, the decision margin jumps 5.8-8.0 logits in one iteration at commitment, and intermediates never surface through the tied readout. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-08-04.
- [Loop-Mamba: A Loop Mamba with Degradation-Aware and Shared Memory for Old Photo Restoration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02346): Loop-Mamba restores old photos by repeatedly applying a degradation-guided Mamba state-evolution operator with shared structural memory to one persistent restoration state, 3 cycles by default; on SynOld it has the best PSNR (30.13), SSIM, FSIM and ODRS among compared methods with fewer FLOPs and MACs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-03.
- [TextNCA: Neural Cellular Automata for Language Modeling via Hierarchical Local Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02050): TextNCA cascades three stages (windows 8, 32, 128) that each iterate shared-weight causal windowed attention; at roughly 30M parameters on WikiText-103 it reaches 60.3 PPL vs 52.8 for Transformer-6L, a non-iterating model with the same schedule comes within +4.1 PPL, and iteration is best at T_s=4. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-08-03.
- [REIMU: Efficient Heterogeneous Hierarchical Reasoning for SSL-Based Speech Deepfake Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00857): On SSL features for speech deepfake detection, REIMU finds that weight-shared recurrence and HRM-style hierarchy alone do not beat single-pass backbones on ASVspoof 2019 and 2021, but a heterogeneous HRM with self-attention and linear-attention modules stays competitive with 10.8% fewer downstream parameters. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-08-01.
- [Retrofitting Recurrent Depth into a Pretrained Language Model: Installation, Extrapolation, Transfer, and Retention at Two Parameter Budgets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11233): Splits Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct into prelude, weight-tied recurrent block and coda; with intermediate-step supervision it computes one task step per loop, extrapolates to roughly 1.5 times its supervised depth, and beats a scratchpad model 84% versus 72%. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-31.
- [ReLoop-UME: Recurrent Depth with Learnable Retrieval Registers for Universal Multimodal Embedding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28751): ReLoop-UME, a multimodal embedding model, runs early layers once, loops a shared retrieval-forming block, then the final mapping layers, with registers carrying evidence across loops; on MMEB-V2 and MRMR it improves retrieval across backbones and runs 44.9x faster than UME-R1 and 1.5x faster than PLUME. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-07-30.
- [Looped Transformers with Source-Centered State Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27656): SCSE removes repeated input injection from looped Transformers: the shared block evolves only the hidden state's deviation from a learned input-conditioned anchor, kept an exact fixed point by a zero-deviation mask, which improves the controlled recurrent quality frontier on WikiText, web-text and LAMBADA. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-07-30.
- [Recursive transformers for semiconductor thermo-mechanical reliability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27251): Compares three weight-sharing recursive Transformers, including a proposed Depth Recursive model and TRM, as surrogates for semiconductor package stress, warpage and a Laplace PDE; the Depth Recursive models give the strongest or near-strongest retrieval accuracy with among the fewest parameters and lowest FLOPs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-07-28.
- [Penelope: Localized Latent Recurrence for Efficient Structured Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.25915): Penelope makes a pretrained decoder-only Transformer run its lower layers once and then loop only a late interval (layers [11,16) of Llama-3.2-1B) over fixed-size memory states; after a CoT-to-latent curriculum, its accuracy is competitive with established latent-reasoning models at lower measured latency. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-07-28.
- [Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22083): Nanbeige4.2-3B is pretrained from scratch on 28T tokens as a Looped Transformer that reuses its layer stack, then post-trained with SFT and RL; it outperforms larger models including Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma4-12B on agentic benchmarks. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-24.
- [Memoir: Should a Model Write to Its Memory While It Thinks?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20792): Memoir asks whether each variable-depth pondering iteration should rewrite the per-sample fast memory it reads; on associative recall with key interference, read-only pondering beats the coupled arm after 240 steps (0.6557 vs 0.5203 recall, 10 of 12 seeds), and both reach 1.0000 after 960 steps. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-07-22.
- [When Does Recurrence Become an Algorithm? Convergence Selection in Weight-Tied Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20594): Trains weight-tied looped transformers on group word problems; training installs a serial frontier that solves about n_train/T_train positions per loop, and weight tying, not expressivity, selects it over the parallel scans untied models learn. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-07-22.
- [LatentMT: Machine Translation with Latent Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18618): LatentMT trains per-language-pair LoRA adapters on a frozen 2.6B-parameter looped LM (Ouro-2.6B-Thinking) run at a fixed number of recurrent steps; across 32 translation directions it matches models three to five times larger, and gains from more steps saturate after the early steps. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-21.
- [Operational Proto-Introspection in Looped Language Models: Reading Correctness Before the Answer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18553): Probes the per-loop hidden states of the 2.6B looped model Ouro-RLTT: from the first 48 reasoning tokens a probe predicts answer correctness with AUROC 0.758 versus 0.515 for token confidence, prefers the correct of two answers 74% of the time, and ranks answers well at layer 8 by the third loop. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-07-20.
- [Mobius Learning: Cyclic Depth Folding in Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17843): Mobius Learning runs each worker's data through a looped Transformer's block groups in a cyclically shifted order, so every group trains in shallow and deep roles; with a 124M modded GPT-2 on 2.5B FineWeb tokens, it reaches lower validation loss than a fixed-order looped Transformer at 6, 10 and 15 passes. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-07-20.
- [Loop the Loopies!](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16051): Loopie comprises two open-source looped MoE Transformers (20B with 2B active, 6B with 0.6B active) that repeat each layer in place; ablations show they outperform vanilla Transformers trained with the same compute budget. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-07-17.
- [Looped Latent Attention: Cross-Loop KV Compression for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15456): Looped Latent Attention, a post-training codec, stores the per-loop KV cache as compact latents and rebuilds loop-specific K/V on read; at matched cache budget it beats head-axis MLA, cross-layer sharing, KV quantization and final-loop reuse. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-07-16.
- [T^2MLR: Transformer with Temporal Middle-Layer Recurrence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.15178): T2MLR fuses a middle-layer state cached from the previous token into an earlier layer at the current token; it beats data- and parameter-matched Transformers, and recurrence over a middle block often beats full-layer recurrence. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-07-16.
- [Per-Token Fixed-Point Convergence in Depth-Recurrent Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.14427): In a 135M-class depth-recurrent Transformer trained with randomized recursion counts, each token's state converges to a fixed point; a training-free exit that halts a token once its output stabilizes attains uniform depth-8 quality at 4.94 average loops, while a trained linear router gives no reduction. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-07-15.
- [DeepLoop: Depth Scaling for Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.13491): DeepLoop derives a residual-scaling rule for looped Transformers that counts repeated visits to shared blocks; in GPT-2 small and medium looped language models it improves validation loss and downstream accuracy once blocks are revisited. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-07-15.
- [The Equilibrium Is the Initialization: Lazy Identity Collapse in Physics-Structured Deep Equilibrium Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11116): On ProofWriter entailment and graph reachability, a port-Hamiltonian DEQ with a learned initialization returns its start point as the equilibrium: bypassing the solver changes test accuracy by +0.00 percentage points in 18 of 19 training runs, which the paper traces to gradient starvation. Category: understanding; focus: related; 2026-07-13.
- [Spectral Margins and Memory Routing in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10681): In a small LayerNorm-based Parcae loop, fixed points are stable because the Jacobian's spectral radius stays below 1, though its distance from 1 shrinks as the carry nears 1; on multi-hop copy, carries frozen at 0.5, 0.02 or 0 match a learned carry at fixed depth, but with sampled depth 0.02 and 0 fail to train. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-07-12.
- [Energy-guided Recursive Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10128): ERM uses Hopfield-type memories of valid local and global structures to assign energies to a recursive model's candidate trajectories, which guide selection and suggest an effective recurrent depth; it reaches 98.97% on Sudoku, 88.04% on PPBench and 99.30% on Maze, and cuts RedPajama-V2 perplexity by 1.74%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-07-11.
- [CHASE: Cache-Hole-Adapted Skip Exit for Looped State-Space Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10110): Loops a shared Mamba (or hybrid Mamba-Transformer) block and adapts Ouro's exit gate; since skipped steps leave cache holes in the recurrent state, CHASE continues training on cache-hole-consistent passes, keeping perplexity close to full computation while executing roughly half of the recurrent steps. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-07-11.
- [Adaptive Depth in Looped Transformers: Diagnosing Learned Halting Gates and Trajectory Readouts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20519): Splits adaptive depth in looped Transformers into trajectory formation and exit readout; fixed-prior depth supervision plus confidence readouts often matches or beats learned halting gates, and Ouro's pretrained gates are competitive but not uniformly Pareto-optimal. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-07-08.
- [Reproducing Recurrent Transformers: The CoTFormer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.19405): Reproduces CoTFormer, which reapplies weight-tied layers while keeping earlier repeats attendable: perplexity results reproduce, adaptive-depth claims are less clean, and looping helps p-hop induction (roughly 0.66 vs 0.4676 test accuracy for a 1×1 Transformer) but not OOD shifted-start counting. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-07-07.
- [Soft Mixture-of-Recursions: Going Deeper with Recursive Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00774): SR-ViT recursively reuses shared intermediate ViT blocks and mixes the outputs of all recursion steps with learned token-wise weights (SoftMoR); on ImageNet-1K, raising recursion depth from T=1 to T=3 improves top-1 accuracy from 79.83% to 82.45% with only 1.1M additional parameters. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-07-01.
- [DiscoLoop: Looping Discrete Embeddings and Continuous Hidden States for Multi-hop Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.00341): Finds that a looped transformer's first loop leaves the two-hop bridge entity decodable but misaligned with its embedding; DiscoLoop adds a decoded-embedding channel between loops and outperforms looped baselines on multi-hop tasks and in pretraining. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-07-01.
- [CHERRY: Compressed Hierarchical Experts with Recurrent Representational Yield](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31796): CHERRY merges adjacent layers of a 48-layer Korean language model into 6 unique blocks, unrolls the middle layers as a recurrent core and heals the result with selected-token supervision; the 227M model reaches loss 2.934 vs 2.926 for a 566M dense model, and MoEE fusion of compressed models reaches 2.789. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-06-30.
- [Bridging the Gap Between Latent and Explicit Reasoning with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31779): LOTUS loops a pretrained LM over padded latent blocks and supervises each latent position with its gold CoT-step token; at 3B scale it closes the gap to explicit CoT while cutting thought-phase latency 2.5x-6.9x. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-06-30.
- [Stabilizing Extrapolation in Looped Transformers via Learned Stochastic Stopping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29983): Traces OOD variance in looped Transformers' length generalization to a spurious correlation between sequence length and loop count; random training loop counts reduce it, and learned stochastic stopping (RL-Halting) often improves the accuracy-stability trade-off on binary addition, Dyck-1, Unique Set and Copy. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-06-29.
- [Flow Reasoning Models: Turning Flows Into Efficient Recurrent Reasoners](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.29150): Flow Reasoning Models feed their own clean-solution prediction back into the same flow denoiser and train it with Fixed-Point Forcing on self-generated states; they solve 99.5%, 100.0% and 99.9% of Sudoku-Extreme, Zebra and Maze-Unique and match the next-best 98.7% on Sudoku-Extreme with 44× fewer inference FLOPs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-06-28.
- [Quantizing Recursive Reasoning Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16237): Quantizing weight-tied recursive puzzle reasoners (TRM, EqR) shows that per-tensor 4-bit activations let a systematic bias accumulate over reuse, cutting Sudoku exact accuracy from 84.1% to 0.0%; per-block activation scaling with MXInt4 restores accuracy across architectures and transfers to ARC-AGI. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-06-25.
- [What Survives When You Compress a Recursive Reasoner for the Edge?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.26488): Compresses recursive reasoning models (TRM, HRM) for edge hardware: pruning, distillation and linear attention drive puzzle-exact accuracy to zero while cell accuracy holds; one recursive cycle matches full-depth accuracy at 6x fewer FLOPs, and calibrated INT4 brings the backbone to 3.3 MB, inside a 4 MB budget. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-06-25.
- [Repeated Shared Access Enables Grokking, but Edit Propagation Depends on an Addressable Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.20737): Crossing loop recurrence with shared memory on synthetic knowledge-graph QA, looped recomputation and memory rereading both cross the OOD grokking barrier a dense transformer fails, but a factual edit reaches 2-hop queries mainly with memory (LMC 0.78-0.92, Dense+Mem 0.71-0.96), weakly in Loop (0.04-0.30). - [Loop-$μ$P: Residual Scaling and Hyperparameter Transfer in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18524): Loop-μP scales each residual branch of a looped Transformer by 1/N for N loops, combined with Depth-μP's L^{-1/2} for depth L, since a shared layer adds positively correlated increments every loop; in language modeling the smallest model's tuned base learning rate stays best for up to 8 loops and 384 executed layers. - [Looped World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18208): LoopWM refines latent environment states by iterating a parameter-shared Transformer block between a prelude and coda, with a spectrally constrained update and Poisson-sampled loop counts; on ScienceWorld text world modelling, the about 1B-parameter model beats claude-opus-4-6-max by 21.2% on EM. - [Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18206): FPRM stabilizes deep looped Transformers with pre-norm layers and residual scaling and halts when the hidden state reaches a fixed point, adapting compute to task difficulty; it is effective on Sudoku, Maze, state-tracking and ARC-AGI. - [LoopCoder-v2: Only Loop Once for Efficient Test-Time Computation Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18023): LoopCoder-v2 trains 7B Parallel Loop Transformer coders on 18T tokens; two loops lift SWE-bench Verified from 43.0 (non-looped) to 64.4, but three or more regress as later-loop gains shrink against a roughly fixed position-offset cost. - [Recursive Scaling in Masked Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18022): R-MDMs apply one shared denoising Transformer L times within each masked-diffusion step; recursion matches substantially larger non-recursive models at matched FLOPs, and entropy-guided rules for loop count and token commits improve the quality–compute frontier on Sudoku, Countdown, RNA and executable math generation. - [Tying the Loop -- Tied Expert Layers in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.16825): Expert Tying shares MoE expert weights across groups of consecutive layers while keeping routing and attention per layer; on OLMoE, Qwen3 and DeepSeek-style MoEs it reduces memory footprint by almost 2x, and tying in groups of four cuts total parameters by up to 52% with negligible quality loss. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-06-15.
- [Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24898): Per-loop cross-entropy through RMSNorm readouts cannot see hidden-state scale, so 44M and 129M looped Transformers without inter-loop normalization reach final norms in the thousands or tens of thousands; scale-visible readouts or norm penalties keep norms in the tens and lower perplexity at matched inference depth. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-06-12.
- [Slots, Transitions, Loops: Learning Composable World Models for ARC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.12316): Loop-OWM encodes ARC grids into color-prototype slots, summarizes demonstrations into task tokens, and applies a shared transition module for 4 recurrent steps; the 10.63M model reaches 68.5 on ARC-1 and 22.5 on ARC-2 (pass@2), above the 18M LoopViT-L at 65.8 and 14.2. - [Rethinking Depth: A study of the Recursive-Transformer for Speech Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09357): Studies Recursive-Transformer ASR encoders, including a Latent-Recursive-Transformer that loops a shared middle block between a prelude and a coda; with a restricted number of loops it performs comparably to standard Transformers while reducing the parameter count by 66%. - [Skip a Layer or Loop It? Learning Program-of-Layers in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06574): Shows that frozen pretrained LLMs admit per-input programs that skip or repeat layer segments, and trains a lightweight predictor of such programs that improves math reasoning accuracy over standard inference, often using fewer layers. - [Test-Time Compute Scaling for ASR with Depth-Conditioned Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04678): LARM loops a shared Transformer block as an ASR acoustic encoder, adding sparse CTC checkpoints, supervision-clock embeddings, FiLM depth conditioning and delayed soft-posterior feedback; on LibriSpeech it improves WER as inference loops increase and is competitive with deeper unshared-parameter baselines. - [LoopMoE: Unifying Iterative Computation with Mixture-of-Experts for Language Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04438): LoopMoE loops an MoE block with iteration- and token-conditioned normalization (IterAdaLN); over a vanilla MoE with identical parameters and FLOPs, its average gain grows from over 1 point at 3B to approximately 3 at 9B. - [CART: Context-Anchored Recurrent Transformer -- A Parameter-Efficient Architecture with Learned Stability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01495): CART loops one shared core block R times over K and V computed once by a multi-layer prelude, with a learned LTI gate for stability; prelude depth P dominates loop count R, and at d=1024 it trails a parameter-matched dense baseline by 1-2% at stored-parameter parity and ~10% at effective-parameter parity. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-31.
- [Looped Transformers with Layer Normalization Provably Learn the Power Method](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.00605): Proves that a looped linear Transformer with layer normalization, trained by gradient descent only for principal component prediction, converges to the power method, each self-attention layer performing one power iteration; a Transformer without LN cannot exactly learn it even with layerwise guidance. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-05-30.
- [Fixed-Point Masked Generative Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.31215): FP-MGMs replace a masked generative denoiser's middle layers with a fixed-point solver over shared attention layers, plus cross-step consistency and warm-starts; on OpenWebText versus MDLM, parameters fall 38.8% and generative perplexity improves from 830.8 to 101.8 at 96 transformer-block forward passes. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-29.
- [Chain-of-Thought and Compressed Looped Transformers: A Memory-Budget Separation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30757): Proves that a looped Transformer whose recurrent state is a small set of latent slots remains a small-space reasoner however long it runs, so under a standard complexity assumption it cannot decide P-complete problems that polynomial-length CoT can; loops carrying state at every input position avoid this limit. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-05-29.
- [Revisiting Padded Transformer Expressivity: Which Architectural Choices Matter and Which Don't](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30523): The paper shows that padded Transformers' expressivity is robust to attention type, width and uniformity, depending mainly on precision and depth; looping adds circuit-like sequential processing: log^d N-looped constant-precision Transformers reach FO-uniform AC^d, growing-precision ones FO-uniform TC^d. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-05-28.
- [Déjà View: Looping Transformers for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30215): DéjàView applies a single looped transformer block to per-view features for K refinement steps in multi-view 3D reconstruction; it matches or beats much larger feed-forward models on five benchmarks and beats an untied per-step variant. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-28.
- [A Dual-Path Architecture for Scaling Compute and Capacity in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.30202): Each layer pairs a deep sublayer re-applied K times with shared parameters and a wide sublayer with an enlarged FFN applied once, mixed by per-token gates; at two FLOP budgets this beats iso-FLOP loop-only and width-only controls with 17-33% fewer parameters than the width-scaled baseline. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-28.
- [Latent Recurrent Transformer: Architecture Exploration, Training Strategies, and Scaling Behavior](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26797): LRT feeds the previous token's high-level hidden state into the next token's layers; at matched effective compute it improves BPB and CORE and matches a three-loop Transformer in BPB, with one forward per token. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-05-26.
- [Stabilizing Recurrent Dynamics for Test-Time Scalable Latent Reasoning in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26733): STARS trains looped LMs with Jacobian spectral radius regularization and random loop sampling so latent states approach stable fixed points, giving reliable test-time scaling on arithmetic and less degradation with deeper recurrence in math reasoning. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-26.
- [Looped Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26106): LoopMDM loops a few early-middle layers of a masked diffusion language model, sampling the loop count in training; it matches same-size MDMs with up to 3.3× fewer training FLOPs, beats them by up to 8.5 points on GSM8K, and scales inference compute by adding loops. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-25.
- [Do Language Models Need Sleep? Offline Recurrence for Improved Online Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26099): An SSM-attention hybrid 'sleeps' before evicting its KV cache, looping its whole block stack N times over the accumulated context to update SSM fast weights, then predicts in one pass; on a cellular-automaton task the no-loop model stays near 10% exact accuracy, while three and four sleep loops exceed 30%. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-05-25.
- [Boosting Inference with Guided Reasoning: Stochastic Exploration for Recursive Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25230): Views TRM inference as approximate inference over latent trajectories: noise in the inner recursion proposes neighbouring trajectories, which the model's early-stopping head reweights in a particle filter; without retraining, Sudoku-Extreme exact-solve accuracy rises from 85.9% to 98.0% and PPBench from 62.5% to 77.9%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-24.
- [Training-Free Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.23872): Loops a contiguous mid-stack block of a frozen checkpoint at inference without training; naive reapplication usually hurts, but damped sub-steps of the block's ODE update help, e.g. +2.64 pp MMLU-Pro on Qwen3-4B-Instruct. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-22.
- [Equilibrium Reasoners: Learning Attractors Enables Scalable Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21488): Equilibrium Reasoners frame iterative latent reasoning as learning task-conditioned attractors and scale depth and breadth at test time; gains track convergence to solution attractors, reaching over 99% on Sudoku-Extreme versus 2.6% for feedforward models. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-20.
- [LT2: Linear-Time Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20670): LT2 replaces softmax attention in looped transformers with linear or sparse attention; looping refines linear-attention memory and widens the sparse receptive field, and hybrid variants match or surpass the standard looped transformer at lower cost. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-05-20.
- [HRM-Text: Efficient Pretraining Beyond Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20613): HRM-Text pretrains a hierarchical recurrent language model with MagicNorm, warmup deep credit assignment and a task-completion objective on instruction-response pairs; a 1B model on 40 billion unique tokens performs competitively with 2-7B open models. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-20.
- [Probabilistic Tiny Recursive Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19943): PTRM injects Gaussian noise at each deep recursion step of a trained TRM to run parallel trajectories and selects among them with its Q head; without retraining, Sudoku-Extreme accuracy rises from 87.4% to 98.75%. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-19.
- [Generative Recursive Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.19376): GRAM makes recursive reasoning models stochastic latent-variable generative models trained by amortized variational inference, scaling inference by recursion depth and parallel trajectory sampling; it beats deterministic recursive baselines on structured and multi-solution reasoning. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-19.
- [One Model, Two Roles: Emergent Specialization in a Shared Recurrent Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.17811): AIR reuses one Transformer for both latent updates of an HRM/TRM-style reasoner and injects the input only into L-updates; on Sudoku-Extreme and Maze, z_H acts as a committed proposal state while z_L keeps local uncertainty, and specialization needs the shared model to tell the two update types apart. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-18.
- [Reshape and Recur: Improving SSMs with Input Reshaping and Depth Recurrence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16048): Reshape and Recur reuses SSM blocks periodically across depth in LRU, S5, LinOSS and LrcSSM on time-series tasks; one block applied 6 times cuts parameters by 5.3-5.9× while staying competitive, and adaptive inference typically picks 2 to 5 repetitions while maintaining classification performance. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-15.
- [One Pass Is Not Enough: Recursive Latent Refinement for Generative Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.15309): RTM swaps the single-pass MLP mapping network of style-based generators for a TRM-style shared block iterated in nested refinement cycles; with IMLE it reaches the highest precision and recall among current state-of-the-art approaches at competitive FID, and it also improves StyleGAN2 and StyleGAN2-ADA. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-14.
- [Solve the Loop: Attractor Models for Language and Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12466): Attractor Models refine a backbone's output embedding by solving for a fixed point with implicit gradients, keeping training memory constant; a 770M model outperforms a 1.3B Transformer trained on twice as many tokens. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-12.
- [Simply Stabilizing the Loop via Fully Looped Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.18797): Fully Looped Transformer injects the previous loop's output into every layer by reusing self-attention, adding no parameters; it curbs residual explosion and gradient oscillation and trains stably up to 12 loop iterations, where baselines collapse. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-05-11.
- [Latent Chain-of-Thought Improves Structured-Data Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11262): Latent chain-of-thought for structured-data transformers compresses query-position hidden states into feedback tokens, appends them to the input and reruns the same transformer; it beats a same-depth baseline on 7/9 time-series datasets (+12.63% average gain) and 23/27 tabular datasets (+3.25% average gain). Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-11.
- [Minimum Neural Weight Norm = Kolmogorov Complexity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10878): Proves that in looped neural networks with constant-precision weights (stated for a looped Transformer block), the smallest weight norm of a network computing a function is asymptotically equivalent to its Kolmogorov complexity divided by its logarithm, linking norm minimization to algorithmic simplicity. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-05-11.
- [LoopVLA: Learning Sufficiency in Recurrent Refinement for Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09948): LoopVLA iterates a shared Transformer block over multimodal tokens, producing a candidate action and a learned sufficiency score at each iteration to decide when to stop; on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus and VLA-Arena it reduces parameters by 45% and improves inference throughput by up to 1.7 times. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-11.
- [LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11011): LoopUS splits a pretrained LLM into encoder, looped reasoning block and decoder, adding a selective gate, random deep supervision and a confidence head for early exit; this improves reasoning-oriented performance without recurrent training from scratch. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-05-10.
- [Sparse Layers are Critical to Scaling Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.09165): Compares dense and MoE transformers with and without looping; Looped-MoE out-scales the standard baseline while dense looped models do not, since routing picks different experts per pass, and loop boundaries are better early-exit points. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-05-09.
- [LoopQ: Quantization for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16343): LoopQ quantizes looped LMs with one shared quantized backbone plus loop-aware activation scaling, cross-loop state alignment and trajectory-aware calibration; under W4A4 it achieves a 67.8% average relative improvement in five-task mean accuracy across four backbones over the strongest static PTQ baseline. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-05-08.
- [Memory-Efficient Looped Transformer: Decoupling Compute from Memory in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07721): MELT, fine-tuned from Ouro, keeps one KV cache per layer that is shared across loops and updated by a learned gate; it outperforms comparable-size LLMs with a similar memory footprint, far smaller than Ouro's. Category: systems; focus: core; 2026-05-08.
- [Revisiting Transformer Layer Parameterization Through Causal Energy Minimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07588): CEM casts weight-tied attention and gated MLPs as gradient steps on energy functions and repeats these steps within a layer; T=2 consistently improves on T=1, recursive CEM attention can beat the Llama baseline with fewer parameters, and simply reapplying the same block gives little or no gain. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-05-08.
- [Bifurcation Models: Learning Set-Valued Solution Maps with Weight-Tied Dynamics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.07277): Bifurcation models iterate a weight-tied update so different initializations converge to different stable equilibria; the paper proves this represents broad set-valued maps with locally Lipschitz branches, and on frustrated Ising models the dynamics find multiple valid equilibria without branch labels. Category: theory; focus: related; 2026-05-08.
- [Transformers Efficiently Perform In-Context Logistic Regression via Normalized Gradient Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06609): Constructs softmax transformers whose layers each run one normalized gradient descent step for in-context logistic regression, and proves that training one self-attention layer under one-step gradient descent supervision and looping it yields such a model, with convergence and OOD guarantees. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-05-07.
- [Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06510): Studying layerwise dynamics in 6 tabular in-context learning models, the paper finds substantial depthwise redundancy that suggests iterative refinement; as a proof of concept, a single Transformer block looped six times uses only 20% of the original model's parameters with comparable performance. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-07.
- [SMolLM: Small Language Models Learn Small Molecular Grammar](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06322): SMolLM, a 53K-parameter weight-shared Transformer, generates novel SMILES with 95% validity on ZINC-250K, outperforming a standard GPT with 10 times more parameters; across passes the same block resolves brackets first, rings second and valence last. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-07.
- [RD-ViT: Recurrent-Depth Vision Transformer for Semantic Segmentation with Reduced Data Dependence Extending the Recurrent-Depth Transformer Architecture to Dense Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.03999): RD-ViT replaces a ViT's unique blocks with one shared block looped T times between prelude and coda blocks, with LTI-stable injection and ACT halting; on ACDC cardiac MRI it beats standard ViT at 10% training data (Dice 0.774 vs 0.762), and its 3D MoE variant reaches Dice 0.812 with 3.0M parameters. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-05-05.
- [State Stream Transformer (SST) V2: Parallel Training of Nonlinear Recurrence for Latent Space Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00206): SST V2 adds an FFN-driven latent state stream at every decoder layer, carried across positions and across repeated full-stack passes on one token; co-trained into a 27B backbone, with an oracle picking one to four passes per token it reaches a 61.11% GPQA-Diamond capacity bound, +15.15 points over a matched baseline. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-04-30.
- [Universal Transformers Need Memory: Depth-State Trade-offs in Adaptive Recursive Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21999): Studies learned memory tokens in a single-block Universal Transformer with ACT on Sudoku-Extreme; without them no configuration reaches non-trivial accuracy, and inverting the halting-router bias to -3 avoids an initialization trap that breaks most runs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-23.
- [Hyperloop Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21254): Hyperloop Transformers loop the middle block and add loop-level hyper-connections with matrix-valued residual streams; across scales they compare well with depth-matched Transformer and mHC baselines while using approximately 50% fewer parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-04-23.
- [How Much Is One Recurrence Worth? Iso-Depth Scaling Laws for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21106): Fits a joint scaling law over an iso-depth pretraining sweep of looped language models and measures a recurrence-equivalence exponent of 0.46, so replacing unique blocks with shared recurrences raises validation loss at matched training compute. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2026-04-22.
- [LoopCTR: Unlocking the Loop Scaling Power for Click-Through Rate Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.19550): LoopCTR, a click-through rate model, loops a shared block between entry and exit blocks with hyper-connected residuals, MoE and supervision at every loop depth; trained with several loops, it beats all baselines even with zero loops at inference, and oracle analysis shows 0.02–0.04 AUC of untapped headroom. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-21.
- [One Step Forward and K Steps Back: Better Reasoning with Denoising Recursion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18839): Denoising Recursion Models mask the target and train a weight-tied TRM-style transformer to undo the corruption over multiple recursive steps, giving a curriculum of intermediate states; on ARC2-Eval with NVARC pretraining, the 14M DRM reaches 24.9 pass@2 versus 21.8 for TRM and 22.6 for the 4B NVARC LLM. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-20.
- [Stability and Generalization in Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15259): A fixed-point analysis of looped transformers proves that models without recall cannot achieve strong input-dependence, while recall with outer normalization yields stable, input-dependent fixed points; small models on chess, sudoku and prefix-sums follow these predictions. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-04-16.
- [Hierarchical vs. Flat Iteration in Shared-Weight Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.14442): HRM-LM replaces independent Transformer layers with a two-speed recurrent pair shared across steps, a Fast module every step and a Slow module every T steps; at ≈1.2B parameters on OpenWebText, a flat Universal Transformer (UniTF) plateaus at ≈7.6 nats across five runs while HRM-LM converges to 4.18. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-04-15.
- [A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.11791): Analyzes latent states of pretrained looped language models; in many, each recurrent-block layer converges to a distinct fixed point and each iteration repeats feedforward-like stages of inference, depending on input injection and normalization. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-04-13.
