- [Reading Human Preference from Looped Transformer Internal States](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09870): Probes hidden states of the looped Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, which runs its layers four times per token, for human preference on HH-RLHF; a linear probe picks the preferred reply 61.5% of the time and a nonlinear network scoring each reply separately 64.9%, so preference is readable but faint. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-04-10.
- [ELT: Elastic Looped Transformers for Visual Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.09168): ELT loops weight-shared transformer blocks for image and video generation and distills the maximum-loop output into intermediate loops for any-time inference; with 4× fewer parameters at iso-inference compute, it reaches FID 2.0 on ImageNet 256×256. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-10.
- [Loom: A Scalable Analytical Neural Computer Architecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08816): Loom runs C programs inside a looped Transformer with analytically derived weights: each pass through 8 layers executes one instruction of a 22-opcode set, repeating until the program counter reaches zero; the default d = 155, n = 1024 machine has 4.7 million parameters and 928 instruction slots. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-04-09.
- [Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07822): Trains recurrent-depth Transformers from scratch on implicit multi-hop knowledge composition; unlike vanilla Transformers they generalize systematically through a three-stage grokking process and extrapolate to deeper compositions with more inference-time iterations, until overthinking degrades predictions. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-04-09.
- [One-Shot Localisation of the Global Minimum of a Noisy One-Dimensional Function: A Controlled Comparison of an Iterative Neural Minimizer, Set Transformers and Classical Estimators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.03614): The Neural Function Minimizer runs a weight-tied read-iterate-update loop for fifteen steps, moving a position and re-reading twenty noisy samples of a one-dimensional function; its regret is 2.90 and 3.12 points of the range lower than a same-size one-pass Set Transformer's (one and two heads). Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-04.
- [Ouroboros: Dynamic Weight Generation for Recursive Transformers via Input-Conditioned LoRA Modulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.02051): Ouroboros adds a Controller hypernetwork that makes each step of a recursive block input-dependent by modulating frozen SVD-initialized LoRA bases; on Qwen2.5-3B cut to Prelude/Recurrent/Coda (17 of 36 layers) it cuts training loss by 43.4% over the 17-layer baseline, but not held-out loss. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-04-02.
- [Exploration of Fast-Slow Latent Recurrence for Train-Short, Test-Long Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.01577): FSRM applies a weight-shared recurrent core several times per observation and carries the latent state across the stream without reset; trained on Dyck sequences of length ≤40, it keeps ≈80% token accuracy up to length 10^5 and generalizes OOD better than recurrent, state-space and Transformer baselines. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-04-02.
- [Associative-State Universal Transformers: Sparse Retrieval Meets Structured Recurrence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.25930): UniMatrix, a Universal Transformer style byte-level LM, reuses one shared matrix-state recurrent block across depth; it slightly beats a parameter-matched Transformer on WikiText-2 (5.084 and 5.083 vs 5.124 bits-per-byte) but stays near chance on associative recall until sparse pointer retrieval reaches 75.6 percent. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-04-01.
- [LA-Sign: Looped Transformers with Geometry-aware Alignment for Skeleton-based Sign Language Recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.29057): LA-Sign reuses a shared encoder-decoder Transformer block recurrently to refine skeleton-based sign representations, regularized by contrastive alignment of skeletal and textual features in adaptive hyperbolic space; it reaches state-of-the-art results on WLASL and MSASL with fewer unique layers. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-03-30.
- [Sparse Growing Transformer: Training-Time Sparse Depth Allocation via Progressive Attention Looping](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.23998): SGT loops only the highest-entropy attention heads and grows this recurrence from deeper to shallower layers during training; it outperforms static block-level looping baselines while cutting the extra training FLOPs over a standard Transformer from approximately 16–20% to 1–3%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-03-25.
- [Thinking Deeper, Not Longer: Memory-Efficient Test-Time Reasoning with Depth-Recurrent Transformers for Compositional Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21676): A shared-weight Transformer block, kept stable for 20+ thinking steps by final-output-only supervision, LayerScale initialization and an identity-biased gate, extrapolates past its training range and comes within two points of fixed-depth Transformers with 4-6.4× more parameters on two sequence tasks. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-03-23.
- [LoopRPT: Reinforcement Pre-Training for Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19714): LoopRPT brings reinforcement pre-training to looped LMs, rewarding each latent loop step against an EMA teacher via noisy latent rollouts and training the exit policy; on Ouro-2.6B it boosts Hard Peak next-token reasoning accuracy by +3.58 while reducing average steps from 3.51 to 2.28. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-03-20.
- [IQuest-Coder-V1 Technical Report](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.16733): Technical report for the IQuest-Coder-V1 dense code models (7B-40B), whose 40B Loop variants run all 80 layers twice with shared parameters, the second iteration gating between global attention over first-iteration KV and local attention; 40B-Loop-Instruct scores 76.2 on SWE-bench Verified against 70.4 for the non-looped 40B-Instruct. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-03-17.
- [SCORE: Replacing Layer Stacking with Contractive Recurrent Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.10544): SCORE replaces stacked layers with one shared block applied for a fixed number of steps through the contractive update ht+1 = (1 - dt) * ht + dt * F(ht); on GNNs for ESOL, MLPs and nanoGPT it generally speeds convergence while cutting parameters, and simple Euler steps give the best cost trade-off. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-03-11.
- [Adaptive Loops and Memory in Transformers: Think Harder or Know More?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08391): Lets each block loop with learned halting and adds gated memory banks; looping mainly helps math, memory banks help commonsense tasks, and combined they beat an iso-FLOP baseline with three times the layers on math. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-03-09.
- [Tiny Autoregressive Recursive Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.08082): Adapts TRM's nested two-stream refinement to causal next-token decoders and compares it with untied depth and Universal Transformer variants at matched block passes on character-level algorithmic tasks; some two-level refinement baselines are strong, but the full Autoregressive TRM gives no reliable gains. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-03-09.
- [Mixture of Universal Experts: Scaling Virtual Width via Depth-Width Transformation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.04971): MoUE reuses a shared pool of universal experts across MoE layers under a fixed activation budget; it beats matched MoE baselines by up to 1.3% and converts existing MoE checkpoints with up to 4.2% gains. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-03-05.
- [PonderLM-3: Adaptive Token-Wise Pondering with Differentiable Masking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.02023): PonderLM-3 adds a router that sets how many PonderLM-2 pondering steps (the last hidden state fed back through the same model) each token gets; a differentiable attention mask in pretraining matches hard stopping at inference, beating recursive or adaptive baselines in perplexity at equal inference FLOPs. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-03-02.
- [AdaPonderLM: Gated Pondering Language Models with Token-Wise Adaptive Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01914): AdaPonderLM, a recurrent LM, learns token-wise halting with iteration-specific MLP gates and reuses KV states of halted tokens; it cuts inference compute by about 10% at comparable perplexity, spending more compute on high-NLL tokens. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-03-02.
- [Turbo Connection: Reasoning as Information Flow from Higher to Lower Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17993): TurboConn routes dense residual connections from higher-layer hidden states of token t into lower layers of token t+1 in fine-tuned pretrained LLMs; it gains 0.9% to over 10% on GSM8K, Parity and multi-step arithmetic, and lifts Qwen-3-1.7B on Parity from 53.78% to 100%. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-02-20.
- [From Growing to Looping: A Unified View of Iterative Computation in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16490): Looped and depth-grown (middle-layer duplication) LLMs share depth-wise signatures of iterative computation; looping a middle block of a depth-grown model at inference, without loop training, raises accuracy on some reasoning primitives by up to 2x. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-02-18.
- [Inner Loop Inference for Pretrained Transformers: Unlocking Latent Capabilities Without Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14759): Inner looping re-applies a middle block range of frozen pretrained LMs at inference, interpolating looped states with earlier ones to limit distribution shift; on Gemma 2-2B, looping layers 10–13 with uniform interpolation raises GSM8K from 25.02 to 26.00, while Llama 3-8B responds less consistently. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-02-16.
- [Tiny Recursive Reasoning with Mamba-2 Attention Hybrid](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12078): Replaces the Transformer blocks inside TRM's recursion with a Mamba-2 + attention hybrid at parameter parity (6.83M vs 6.86M); on ARC-AGI-1 the hybrid raises pass@2 by +2.0% (45.88% vs 43.88%) and leads by +4.75% at pass@100, with pass@1 parity. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-02-12.
- [SpiralFormer: Looped Transformers Can Learn Hierarchical Dependencies via Multi-Resolution Recursion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11698): SpiralFormer runs a looped Transformer's shared core at a different sequence resolution each iteration, coarse to fine; from 160M to 1.4B it beats looped and non-looped baselines in parameter and compute efficiency. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2026-02-12.
- [LoopFormer: Elastic-Depth Looped Transformers for Latent Reasoning via Shortcut Modulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11451): Trains one looped Transformer for many depths via time and step-size conditioning and a shortcut-consistency loss; it performs well on language modeling and reasoning under tight compute budgets and improves as the budget grows. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-02-11.
- [Prioritize the Process, Not Just the Outcome: Rewarding Latent Thought Trajectories Improves Reasoning in Looped Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10520): RLTT replaces GRPO's final-state credit with reward spread over the whole latent thought trajectory of looped LMs; on Ouro-Thinking it raises mean math accuracy over GRPO by +5.8% at 1.4B and +10.9% at 2.6B. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-02-11.
- [Step-resolved data attribution for looped transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10097): Step-Decomposed Influence (SDI) unrolls a looped Transformer to split TracIn data attribution into per-iteration influence scores, using TensorSketch so per-example gradients are never materialised; on looped GPT-style models and algorithmic tasks it matches full-gradient baselines with low error. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-02-10.
- [Looping Back to Move Forward: Recursive Transformers for Efficient and Flexible Large Multimodal Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.09080): RecursiveVLM loops a multimodal model's LLM backbone, adding a Recursive Connector that fuses intermediate-layer states per modality and a Monotonic Recursion Loss; it gains +3% over standard Transformers and +7% over vanilla recursive baselines. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-02-09.
- [Understanding Dynamic Compute Allocation in Recurrent Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08864): ANIRA's decider sets each token's number of recurrent-block iterations from the prelude or by online halting; on tasks of controllable difficulty, allocation tracks complexity without difficulty labels (Spearman up to +0.666), yet accuracy drops sharply at unseen input sizes. Category: depth; focus: core; 2026-02-09.
- [Emergent Search and Backtracking in Latent Reasoning Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08100): Decoding looped Huginn-0125's answer beliefs at every recurrence step on multiple-choice QA reveals exploration, tentative commitment, then convergence or backtracking; backtracking occurs in 32% of instances with a 34% accuracy gain, and implausible distractors shorten exploration by 54%. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-02-08.
- [Recurrent-Depth VLA: Implicit Test-Time Compute Scaling of Vision-Language-Action Models via Latent Iterative Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.07845): RD-VLA gives a VLA a weight-tied recurrent action head that stops on latent convergence; tasks failing at one iteration exceed 90 percent success with four, and inference is up to 80x faster than reasoning VLAs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-02-08.
- [Multimodal Latent Reasoning via Hierarchical Visual Cues Injection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.05359): HIVE builds a multimodal model on Huginn's recurrent core and injects ViT features from layers 6, 12, 18 and 24 into the first recurrent iterations, one tier per step; on ScienceQA-Img accuracy rises from 32.82% at r=1 to 91.57% at r=32, vs 89.39% without hierarchical cues. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-02-05.
- [Lipschitz Multiscale Deep Equilibrium Models: A Theoretically Guaranteed and Accelerated Approach](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.03297): Lipschitz MDEQ modifies the multiscale DEQ so hyperparameters set the Lipschitz constant of its weight-tied fixed-point mapping, guaranteeing forward and backward fixed-point convergence; on CIFAR-10 classification it gives up to a 4.75× speed-up for a minor drop in accuracy. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-02-03.
- [LoopViT: Scaling Visual ARC with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.02156): Loop-ViT iterates a weight-tied hybrid convolution-attention block on ARC-AGI grids and at inference halts once predictive entropy is low; the 18M model reaches 65.8% on ARC-AGI-1, above 73M-parameter ensembles. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-02-02.
- [Beyond What Seems Necessary: Hidden Gains from Scaling Training-Time Reasoning Length under Outcome Supervision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00927): Shows in theory and experiments that under outcome-only supervision, OOD performance keeps improving as training-time reasoning length (looped-Transformer loop count, RL token budget) grows past ID saturation; on a synthetic induction task, ID accuracy saturates around 2 loops while OOD accuracy keeps rising. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-01-31.
- [Depth-Recurrent Attention Mixture (Dreamer): Giving Latent Reasoning the Attention it Deserves](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21582): Dreamer combines sequence attention, depth attention and sparse expert attention in a depth-recurrent model; against FLOP-, parameter- and memory-matched baselines it needs 2 to 8x fewer training tokens for the same accuracy on language reasoning. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2026-01-29.
- [Scale-Consistent State-Space Dynamics via Fractal of Stationary Transformations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19551): FROST iterates one weight-tied ResNet or ViT transition as a contractive, self-similar state-space update so intermediate states approximate the final one, making ranking-based halting stable; on CIFAR-100, accuracy rises from 45.39% at average depth 4.37 to 61.99% at full depth 16.00. Category: applications; focus: related; 2026-01-27.
- [Loop as a Bridge: Can Looped Transformers Truly Link Representation Space and Natural Language Outputs?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.10242): Tests whether looping lets Ouro close the gap between internal representations and verbal outputs; more loops narrow it partly because representational knowledge degrades, and injected concepts are perceived only in the final loop. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2026-01-15.
- [Energy-Entropy Regularization: The True Power of Minimal Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.09588): Energy-Entropy Regularization uses Tsallis entropy and Hamiltonian dynamics to reshape the loss landscape of single-head looped Transformers; with it, a single-head looped Transformer with model dimension d = 8 solves the induction head task with input sequence length of 1000 tokens. Category: training; focus: core; 2026-01-14.
- [Context-Free Recognition with Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.01754): Proves that looped transformers with O(log(N)) looping layers and O(N^6) padding symbols recognize all context-free languages, and unambiguous CFLs need only O(N^3) padding; empirically, looped and padded transformers recognize CFLs better than fixed-depth transformers. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-01-05.
- [Context Collapse: In-Context Learning and Model Collapse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.00923): For in-context linear regression with a linear Transformer whose layers all share one weight matrix, the thesis reduces the forward pass to preconditioned gradient descent and proves the optimal solution gains a skew-symmetric component above a critical context length; it also studies model collapse. Category: theory; focus: core; 2026-01-01.
- [Block-Recurrent Dynamics in Vision Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.19941): Raptor rewrites pretrained ViTs as a few weight-tied blocks, each applied recurrently over a contiguous phase of depth; with only 2 blocks it recovers 96% of DINOv2 ImageNet-1k linear probe accuracy at equivalent runtime, and its depth dynamics converge into class-dependent angular basins. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-12-23.
- [Universal Reasoning Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14693): Analyzing Universal Transformer variants, the paper attributes ARC-AGI gains mainly to the recurrent inductive bias and strong nonlinearity; URM adds short convolution and truncated backpropagation through loops to a looped 4-layer Transformer and reaches 53.8% pass@1 on ARC-AGI 1 and 16.0% on ARC-AGI 2. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-12-16.
- [VersatileFFN: Achieving Parameter Efficiency in LLMs via Adaptive Wide-and-Deep Reuse](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.14531): VersatileFFN reuses one FFN both as sub-experts (width path) and recursively with a learned per-token loop count (depth path), mixed by a difficulty-aware gate; at the 1.21B scale it reaches 60.47% average zero-shot accuracy versus 59.65% for MoE and 60.05% for 6-Loop. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-12-16.
- [Improving Recursive Transformers with Mixture of LoRAs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12880): ModernALBERT, a recursive Transformer encoder sharing layer parameters within groups, adds token-routed LoRA experts inside the shared FFN (Mixture of LoRAs); its 50M to 120M models are state of the art among compact models on GLUE, SQuAD-v2 and BEIR and surpass larger fully parameterised baselines. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2025-12-14.
- [Closed-Loop Transformers: Autoregressive Modeling as Iterative Latent Equilibrium](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.21882): Equilibrium Transformers add a module to every layer that runs proximal gradient descent on a learned energy to refine the hidden state before each token is emitted; on binary cumulative parity they beat standard Transformers by +3.28% on average at challenging lengths, up to +8.07%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-11-26.
- [Latent Reasoning in TRMs is Secretly a Policy Improvement Operator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.16886): Frames latent recursion in Tiny Recursive Models as policy improvement and supervises each recursive step with an intermediate target from a discrete diffusion schedule, dropping the halting head; on TRM this avoids dead compute and cuts total forward passes by 18x while maintaining performance. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-11-21.
- [Think-at-Hard: Dynamic Looped Transformers for Improved Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.08577): TaH re-iterates a Qwen3 backbone only on tokens that a lightweight neural decider flags as likely wrong, using duo-causal attention over earlier positions and shallower iterations; at identical parameter counts it beats always-iterate baselines by 3.8-4.4% while skipping iterations on 93% of tokens. Category: depth; focus: core; 2025-11-11.
- [ScaleNet: Scaling up Pretrained Neural Networks with Incremental Parameters](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18431): ScaleNet deepens pretrained ViTs by inserting layers that share parameter tensors with corresponding pretrained layers, plus small parallel adapters per layer; a 2× depth-scaled DeiT-Base gains 7.42% accuracy over training from scratch on ImageNet-1K with only one-third of the training epochs. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-10-21.
- [ReXMoE: Reusing Experts with Minimal Overhead in Mixture-of-Experts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17483): ReXMoE lets each MoE router pick experts from a group of adjacent layers, so one expert can be reused at several depths, and grows the candidate pool during training; on MoE-2.3BA0.3B, the 4-layer-group ReXMoE raises average downstream accuracy from 49.15% to 50.23%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-10-20.
- [Efficient Parallel Samplers for Recurrent-Depth Models and Their Connection to Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.14961): A diffusion forcing sampler for recurrent-depth models decodes new tokens at every forward pass and keeps refining their latent states in parallel through the recurrence; applied to an existing 3.5B recurrent-depth Transformer without any tuning, it gives up to a 5x speedup. Category: systems; focus: core; 2025-10-16.
- [On the Reasoning Abilities of Masked Diffusion Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13117): Proves that in the finite-precision log-width setting masked diffusion language models are equivalent to polynomially-padded looped transformers, which repeat a middle block of layers; MDMs can also solve all problems CoT transformers can and are more efficient on some classes, including regular languages. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-10-15.
- [Dr.LLM: Dynamic Layer Routing in LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.12773): Dr.LLM equips a frozen pretrained LLM with lightweight per-layer routers that skip, execute, or repeat each block, trained on MCTS-derived layer configurations; on ARC and DART it improves accuracy by up to +3.4%p while saving 5 layers per example on average. Category: depth; focus: core; 2025-10-14.
- [DND: Boosting Large Language Models with Dynamic Nested Depth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11001): DND adds a router at the end of each intermediate layer of a pretrained LLM; tokens it selects pass through the same layer again and the result is fused with the first-pass output; integrated in post-training, it boosts dense Qwen3-1.7B by 1.88% and MoE Qwen3-30B-A3B by 0.87%. Category: depth; focus: core; 2025-10-13.
- [What Makes Looped Transformers Perform Better Than Non-Recursive Ones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.10089): The paper attributes the advantage of looped Transformers (Looped-Attn) over non-recursive ones to a conjectured landscape-level bias toward steep River-V-Valleys, and proposes SHIFT, which trains Single-Attn first and then switches to Looped-Attn to accelerate training with comparable performance. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2025-10-11.
- [MeSH: Memory-as-State-Highways for Recursive Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07739): MeSH gives recursive Transformers an explicit memory buffer and lightweight routers that vary computation across iterations; on Pythia (160M-6.9B) it beats recursive baselines, and at 1.4B it tops the larger non-recursive model by +1.06% average downstream accuracy with 33% fewer non-embedding parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2025-10-09.
- [Encode, Think, Decode: Scaling test-time reasoning with recursive latent thoughts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.07358): Encode-Think-Decode (ETD) mid-trains OLMo-2 1B Base to iterate a 4-layer block of reasoning-relevant layers between 7 encoder and 5 decoder layers, adding no parameters or data; it gains on 17 reasoning benchmarks, including +28.4% relative accuracy on GSM8K and +36% on MATH. Category: training; focus: core; 2025-10-08.
- [Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04871): TRM, a single 2-layer network that recursively refines a latent state and an answer, generalizes better than HRM on puzzles; with 7M parameters it reaches 45% on ARC-AGI-1 and 8% on ARC-AGI-2. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-10-06.
- [Two-Scale Latent Dynamics for Recurrent-Depth Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23314): In looped blocks of a recurrent-depth Transformer, steps grow smaller and more orthogonal over training while states drift more across blocks; exiting on the second-order difference in step size beats Geiping et al.'s KL-divergence exit and a first-order rule in performance, stability and time-efficiency. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2025-09-27.
- [PonderLM-2: Pretraining LLM with Latent Thoughts in Continuous Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.23184): PonderLM-2 feeds each position's last hidden state back into the same model as a latent thought, with the same positional encoding, to predict the next token; at identical inference cost, PonderLM-2-Pythia-1.4B pretrained on 300B Pile tokens surpasses vanilla Pythia-2.8B trained on the same data. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2025-09-27.
- [A Formal Comparison Between Chain of Thought and Latent Thought](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25239): Formally compares looped Transformers (latent thought) with chain of thought: latent thought admits more efficient parallel computation than inherently sequential CoT, while CoT's stochastic decoding enables approximate counting and sampling, indicating which tasks suit depth-driven recursion. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-09-25.
- [Beyond Memorization: Extending Reasoning Depth with Recurrence, Memory and Test-Time Compute Scaling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.16745): On a 1D cellular-automata benchmark with disjoint train and test rules, 4-layer Transformers, LSTMs and SSMs fail as more reasoning steps are needed; Adaptive Computation Time, repeating layers until a learned halt, adds roughly +1 depth of state prediction without new parameters, while GRPO and CoT go further. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2025-08-22.
- [Deep Equilibrium Convolutional Sparse Coding for Hyperspectral Image Denoising](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15553): DECSC casts the proximal-gradient iterations of convolutional sparse coding, with an embedded Swin Transformer, as one weight-tied layer solved to a fixed point by Anderson acceleration; on 50 ICVL test HSIs with non-i.i.d. Gaussian noise of σ in [0, 95], its 45.64 PSNR is the best among compared methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-08-21.
- [AbbIE: Autoregressive Block-Based Iterative Encoder for Efficient Sequence Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08567): AbbIE loops a middle Body of Transformer blocks between a Head and a Tail, carrying the input through the residual stream; trained with only 2 iterations, it upward generalizes to more test-time iterations, improving zero-shot in-context learning by up to 12% and perplexity by up to 5% at up to 350M parameters. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2025-07-11.
- [Latent Chain-of-Thought? Decoding the Depth-Recurrent Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02199): Probing Huginn-3.5B with Logit Lens and Coda Lens on arithmetic finds little evidence of latent CoT and probing results that shift sharply across recurrent blocks; on GSM8K without CoT, 4 to 32 recurrent steps lift accuracy only from 3.11 to 4.93, far below 24.87/38.13 with explicit CoT. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2025-07-02.
- [Energy-Based Transformers are Scalable Learners and Thinkers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.02092): Energy-Based Transformers predict by gradient descent on a learned energy over input-prediction pairs; versus Transformer++, they show up to 35% higher training scaling rate and 29% more gain from System 2 Thinking on language tasks. Category: adjacent; focus: related; 2025-07-02.
- [Hierarchical Reasoning Model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.21734): HRM couples a slow high-level and a fast low-level recurrent module; with 27 million parameters and 1000 training samples, it nearly solves complex Sudoku and large mazes and beats larger models on ARC. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-06-26.
- [Chain-of-Experts: Unlocking the Communication Power of Mixture-of-Experts Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18945): Chain-of-Experts iterates each MoE layer, re-routing tokens among its experts with a dedicated router per iteration; under fixed compute it cuts math validation loss from 1.20 to 1.12 versus standard MoE, and 2x iterations match 3x expert selections with 17.6-42% less memory than other scaling strategies. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-06-23.
- [Beyond Parameters: Exploring Virtual Logic Depth for Scaling Laws](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.18233): Virtual logical depth reuses layers in sequence, cycle or inverse-cycle patterns to add effective depth without new parameters; knowledge capacity stays nearly unchanged while reasoning improves, e.g. the cycle pattern raises a 4-layer model's accuracy from 46.3% to 70.7% with a VLD factor of 5. Category: scaling; focus: core; 2025-06-23.
- [DiffusionBlocks: Block-wise Neural Network Training via Diffusion Interpretation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.14202): DiffusionBlocks trains each residual block independently as a denoiser for its own noise range; on the recurrent-depth model Huginn it replaces training over an average of 32 recurrent iterations with single-pass denoiser training, keeps iterative inference, and raises LM1B MAUVE from 0.49 to 0.70. Category: training; focus: core; 2025-06-17.
- [PonderLM: Pretraining Language Models to Ponder in Continuous Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.20674): PonderLM feeds the probability-weighted sum of token embeddings back into the same model for several forward passes per token, learned by self-supervised pretraining; PonderPythia-2.8B surpasses Pythia-6.9B and rivals Pythia-12B. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2025-05-27.
- [Recurrent Self-Attention Dynamics: An Energy-Agnostic Perspective from Jacobians](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.19458): Jacobian analysis of looped self-attention (AKOrN and ItrSA, mostly on Sudoku): normalization curbs SA's Lipschitzness and complex Jacobian eigenvalues, normalized dynamics sit near a critical state that signals high inference performance, and Jacobians yield regularizers and a pseudo-energy. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-05-26.
- [Exact Expressive Power of Transformers with Padding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.18948): Proves that averaging-hard-attention transformers with polynomial padding recognize exactly FO-uniform TC^0, and that looping a middle block O(log^d n) times raises this to exactly FO-uniform TC^d, so polylogarithmic looping with polynomial padding reaches FO-uniform NC. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-05-25.
- [LARES: Latent Reasoning for Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.16865): LARES iterates a core-block after a pre-block so every latent reasoning step refines all item tokens of a user sequence, training with self-supervised alignment and then RL; it beats all baselines on four datasets and raises FMLP-Rec's NDCG@10 by 15.3% on Instrument and 21.4% on Scientific. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-05-22.
- [Intra-Layer Recurrence in Transformers for Language Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.01855): Intra-Layer Recurrence (ILR) repeats individual layers of a LLaMA-style decoder within one forward pass according to a per-layer reuse map; reusing earlier layers helps most, and the [4,2,1,1] map lowers small-model perplexity from 16.57 to 14.62 with NoPE and from 14.38 to 13.63 with ALiBi. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-05-03.
- [Fixed-Point RNNs: Interpolating from Diagonal to Dense](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10799): Fixed-Point RNNs compute a dense linear RNN as the fixed point of a parallelizable diagonal linear RNN, iterated to convergence, so iterations trade expressivity for efficiency at fixed parameters; they set state-of-the-art results on state-tracking benchmarks A5 and S5 and match baselines on copying. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2025-03-13.
- [A Little Depth Goes a Long Way: The Expressive Power of Log-Depth Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.03961): Proves that looped transformers repeating middle layers Θ(log n) times recognize regular languages and solve graph connectivity, which fixed-depth transformers cannot under standard conjectures; growing depth is more efficient than growing width or chain-of-thought steps. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-03-05.
- [Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent with Chain of Thought](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21212): Proves that with CoT a one-layer linear Transformer learns multi-step gradient descent in context, but without CoT only one step; the same technique shows looped Transformers reach strictly lower asymptotic loss than a non-looped one-layer Transformer on in-context linear regression when L≥2. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-02-28.
- [CODI: Compressing Chain-of-Thought into Continuous Space via Self-Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.21074): CODI jointly trains explicit-CoT teacher and implicit-CoT student tasks, aligning a designated token's hidden states to compress CoT into continuous space; at GPT-2 scale it matches explicit CoT on GSM8k with 3.1x compression. Category: adjacent; focus: related; 2025-02-28.
- [Reasoning with Latent Thoughts: On the Power of Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.17416): Shows that a k-layer transformer looped L times nearly matches a kL-layer model on synthetic reasoning and is competitive on language-model reasoning tasks, and proves T loops can simulate T steps of CoT. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-02-24.
- [Inner Thinking Transformer: Leveraging Dynamic Depth Scaling to Foster Adaptive Internal Thinking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.13842): ITT turns every other layer into a looped layer whose learned routers send selected tokens through extra steps of the same layer, accumulated by residual thinking connections; with 162M parameters it reaches 96.5% of a 466M Transformer's performance, saves 43.2% of training data and beats Transformer and Loop variants on 11 benchmarks. Category: depth; focus: core; 2025-02-19.
- [Zero Token-Driven Deep Thinking in LLMs: Unlocking the Full Potential of Existing Parameters via Cyclic Refinement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.12214): Zero Token Transformer keeps the first and last layers out of parameter cycling, loops only the middle layers, and adds per-cycle zero tokens with trainable keys whose attention scores guide each cycle and trigger early exit; under a 6-cycle budget it averages 33.52 versus 32.79 for cycling all layers. Category: depth; focus: core; 2025-02-17.
- [Hyper-SET: Designing Transformers via Hyperspherical Energy Minimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.11646): Hyper-SET derives a weight-shared recurrent-depth Transformer layer from iterative energy minimization on the hypersphere; with fewer parameters it is competitive or better on Sudoku, image classification and masked image modeling, and gains more than a Transformer when Sudoku test iterations grow to 2× training. Category: applications; focus: related; 2025-02-17.
- [Enhancing Auto-regressive Chain-of-Thought through Loop-Aligned Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.08482): RELAY aligns each iteration of a looped Transformer with one chain-of-thought step and supervises every iteration, keeping length generalization while producing explicit reasoning chains; its chains for problems beyond the training length fine-tune an auto-regressive model and improve its performance. Category: training; focus: core; 2025-02-12.
- [Recursive Inference Scaling: A Winning Path to Scalable Inference in Language and Multimodal Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07503): RINS splits a model into two equal blocks and recursively applies the first to its own output before the second; at matched training compute it outperforms +55 other recursion variants in language modeling, improves data scaling exponents and limits, and adds +2% 0-shot ImageNet accuracy for SigLIP-B/16. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-02-11.
- [Implicit Language Models are RNNs: Balancing Parallelization and Expressivity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.07827): Implicit Mamba2 and Llama3 models self-iterate the stack to an approximate fixed point, gaining RNN-like non-linear state transitions that solve the S5 word problem; with a bounded-then-free iteration curriculum up to 1.3B parameters and 207B tokens, they beat explicit counterparts on standard benchmarks. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2025-02-10.
- [DeltaLLM: Compress LLMs with Low-Rank Deltas between Shared Weights](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.18596): DeltaLLM compresses pretrained LLMs by sharing weights between layers in subsequent Transformer blocks and adding low-rank delta matrices trained on approximately 30M-40M tokens; DeltaLLAMA and DeltaPHI cut parameters by 12% while retaining 90% of base Llama and Phi performance. Category: training; focus: related; 2025-01-30.
- [StagFormer: Time Staggering Transformer Decoding for RunningLayers In Parallel](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15665): StagFormer lets a later Transformer stack see earlier-stack outputs only for past tokens, so stacks run in parallel during decoding; when its 2 staggered 18-layer stacks share all weights except cross-attention, it reaches 3.896 Pile perplexity vs 4.026 for the 18-layer and 3.780 for the 36-layer baseline. Category: systems; focus: core; 2025-01-26.
- [Neural Algorithmic Reasoning for Hypergraphs with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.10688): Proves by construction that a looped Transformer with constant layers and constant feature dimensions simulates hypergraph algorithms: Dijkstra, BFS and DFS through a mechanism that degrades the incidence matrix to an adjacency matrix, and Helly's algorithm through a hyperedge-aware encoding. Category: theory; focus: core; 2025-01-18.
- [Training Large Language Models to Reason in a Continuous Latent Space](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.06769): Coconut feeds the last hidden state back as the next input embedding rather than decoding it into a token; these continuous thoughts can encode alternative next steps, and Coconut outperforms CoT on search-heavy logical reasoning. Category: adjacent; focus: related; 2024-12-09.
- [On the Role of Depth and Looping for In-Context Learning with Task Diversity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.21698): For in-context linear regression with condition numbers in [1, κ], proves log(κ) (or √κ) lower bounds on linear attention layers; multilayer Transformers attain them yet are not robust even to O(e^{-L}) shifts, while Looped Transformers attain them, are provably robust, and alone have loss monotonic in depth. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-29.
- [Relaxed Recursive Transformers: Effective Parameter Sharing with Layer-wise LoRA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.20672): Converts pretrained LLMs into Recursive Transformers that loop one shared block, optionally relaxed with depth-wise LoRA; recursive Gemma 1B beats TinyLlama 1.1B, Pythia 1B and distillation baselines and recovers most of Gemma 2B's performance. Category: training; focus: core; 2024-10-28.
- [ALTA: Compiler-Based Analysis of Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18077): ALTA compiles programs with loops into Transformers whose layers share all attention and MLP weights, including Universal Transformers with dynamic halting; it builds length-invariant parity and addition and a SCAN solution, and uses execution-trace supervision to study why end-to-end training misses them. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-23.
- [Advancing the Understanding of Fixed Point Iterations in Deep Neural Networks: A Detailed Analytical Study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11279): For a looped network repeatedly applying one layer g(Wx+b), gives a sufficient condition for multiple fixed points depending on the input region, extends it to robust fixed points, and shows such networks may have 2^d robust fixed points (d: feature dimension) under polynomial or exponential activations. Category: theory; focus: related; 2024-10-15.
- [Bypassing the Exponential Dependency: Looped Transformers Efficiently Learn In-context by Multi-step Gradient Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11268): Proves that linear looped Transformers implement multi-step gradient descent efficiently for in-context learning on linear vector generation: with a constant input condition number, e.g. n = O(d), they reach small error, avoiding the n = exp(Ω(T)) examples earlier results needed for T loops. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-15.
- [Looped ReLU MLPs May Be All You Need as Practical Programmable Computers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09375): Proves by construction that a looped 23-layer ReLU-MLP can emulate the SUBLEQ instruction and so act as a programmable computer, more efficiently than a looped Transformer, indicating that simple modules are more expressive than expected. Category: theory; focus: related; 2024-10-12.
- [Can Looped Transformers Learn to Implement Multi-step Gradient Descent for In-context Learning?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08292): Proves that for in-context linear regression, the global minimizer of a linear looped Transformer's training loss implements multi-step preconditioned gradient descent, and that gradient flow converges fast despite non-convexity; synthetic experiments agree. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-10.
- [On Logical Extrapolation for Mazes with Recurrent and Implicit Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.03020): Weight-tied RNNs and implicit networks that solve larger mazes by iterating longer lose accuracy when the start may have several neighbors or the maze has cycles; one RNN matches deadend-filling on 98.8% of 143k test mazes, and models can be correct while converging to limit cycles, not fixed points. Category: applications; focus: related; 2024-10-03.
- [On Expressive Power of Looped Transformers: Theoretical Analysis and Enhancement via Timestep Encoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.01405): Derives approximation rates for looped Transformers, revealing a limitation specific to looping, and adds per-loop scaling parameters conditioned on timestep encoding; in experiments more loops improve performance and timestep encoding adds further gains. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-10-02.
- [Looped Transformers for Length Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15647): Trains looped decoder-only Transformers on tasks with known iterative RASP-L solutions, supervising only the final answer after an input-dependent number of steps; adapting the step count at test time improves length generalization. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-09-24.
- [Loop Neural Networks for Parameter Sharing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.14199): Loop Neural Network loops GPT-2 Transformer layers with a residual update at each iteration; a model with 6 layers looped 6 times (81M parameters) reaches validation loss 3.11 on OpenWebText, comparable to 3.12 for the 12-layer GPT-2 124M. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2024-09-21.
- [On the Design Space Between Transformers and Recursive Neural Nets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01531): Formalizes Neural Data Routers, a Universal Transformer variant sharing parameters across layers, and Continuous Recursive Neural Networks as repeated application of one shared function, showing these strong algorithmic generalizers bridge Transformers and recursive neural nets, and discusses limits. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-09-03.
- [MoEUT: Mixture-of-Experts Universal Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16039): MoEUT is a shared-layer Transformer with mixture-of-experts feedforward and attention layers, layer grouping and peri-layernorm; it slightly outperforms standard Transformers on language modeling tasks such as BLiMP and PIQA using less compute and memory. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2024-05-25.
- [Subhomogeneous Deep Equilibrium Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00720): Proves that deep equilibrium models built from subhomogeneous operators have unique fixed points, via nonlinear Perron-Frobenius theory and weaker weight assumptions than monotone-operator DEQs; SubDEQs need fewer fixed-point iterations than MonDEQ and are tested on feedforward, convolutional and graph networks. Category: theory; focus: related; 2024-03-01.
- [MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14905): MobileLLM builds deep-and-thin sub-billion LMs with embedding sharing and grouped-query attention, gaining 2.7%/4.3% accuracy over prior 125M/350M models; MobileLLM-LS computes each Transformer block twice in a row (immediate block-wise weight sharing), adding 0.7%/0.8% with no increase in model size. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2024-02-22.
- [AlgoFormer: An Efficient Transformer Framework with Algorithmic Structures](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13572): AlgoFormer puts a weight-shared looped transformer between a pre- and a post-transformer, mirroring preprocess-iterate-postprocess algorithms; constructions show it can run gradient descent and Newton's method, and on IWSLT 2015 German-English it scores 14.72 BLEU versus 9.30 standard and 10.56 vanilla looped. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-02-21.
- [Simulation of Graph Algorithms with Looped Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.01107): Proves by construction that a looped transformer with extra graph-reading attention heads simulates BFS, DFS, Dijkstra and Kosaraju's algorithm with parameters independent of graph size, within finite-precision limits, and is Turing complete at constant width. Category: theory; focus: core; 2024-02-02.
- [Investigating Recurrent Transformers with Dynamic Halt](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.00976): Compares depth-wise Universal Transformer recurrence with chunk-wise Temporal Latent Bottleneck recurrence and proposes GUT, a gated UT with global mean-based dynamic halting; GUT generally beats UT on ListOps and Logical Inference, while chunk-wise recurrence is more robust in flip-flop LM and length generalization. Category: depth; focus: core; 2024-02-01.
- [Looped Transformers are Better at Learning Learning Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12424): Trains a looped transformer with input injection to solve in-context data-fitting problems such as linear regression; it performs comparably to a standard transformer while using less than 10% of the parameters. Category: theory; focus: core; 2023-11-21.
- [CoTFormer: A Chain-of-Thought Driven Architecture with Budget-Adaptive Computation Cost at Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.10845): CoTFormer re-applies the same layers several times and lets each pass attend to tokens from earlier passes, like chain-of-thought; it approaches much larger models, and a token-wise adaptive-depth variant cuts compute without losing accuracy. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2023-10-16.
- [Adaptivity and Modularity for Efficient Generalization Over Task Complexity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08866): Hyper-UT, a Universal Transformer with per-token ACT, uses hyper-modules to build each layer's weights from a weight-embedding pool shared across layers; it generalizes better to more computation steps on conditional pointer value retrieval and matches ViT on image recognition with over 70% average savings. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2023-10-13.
- [Sparse Universal Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.07096): Adds sparse mixture-of-experts and stick-breaking dynamic halting to the Universal Transformer, matching strong baselines on WMT'14 with half the computation and parameters; halting saves around 50% inference computation on formal language tasks with little loss. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2023-10-11.
- [Federated Deep Equilibrium Learning: Harnessing Compact Global Representations to Enhance Personalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15659): FeDEQ gives federated clients a shared deep equilibrium layer, solved by fixed-point iteration, followed by personalized explicit layers, jointly trained via ADMM; it matches state-of-the-art personalized FL while cutting communication by up to 4 times and training memory by 1.5 times. Category: applications; focus: related; 2023-09-27.
- [Revisiting Implicit Models: Sparsity Trade-offs Capability in Weight-tied Model for Vision Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08013): Revisiting implicit models on vision tasks, the paper finds weight-tied models, which reuse one layer across depth, more effective, stable and efficient than DEQ variants, adds distinct sparse masks to the tied layers to raise capacity, and gives depth, width and sparsity guidelines. Category: applications; focus: related; 2023-07-16.
- [Beyond Universal Transformer: block reusing with adaptor in Transformer for automatic speech recognition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13072): BRST reuses one Transformer block 12 times in the encoder and one 6 times in the decoder of a CTC-attention speech recognizer, adding a small adapter module (ADM) after each reuse; on AISHELL-1 it reaches 9.3%/6.63% CER with 7.6M/8.3M parameters without/with the ADM. Category: applications; focus: related; 2023-03-23.
- [Looped Transformers as Programmable Computers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.13196): Shows that a looped 13-layer transformer with programmed weights, reading instructions and memory from its input, emulates a small instruction-set computer and runs a calculator, linear algebra routines and in-context learning algorithms. Category: theory; focus: core; 2023-01-30.
- [Lightweight and Flexible Deep Equilibrium Learning for CSI Feedback in FDD Massive MIMO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.15079): Builds CSI feedback for FDD massive MIMO from implicit equilibrium blocks, fixed-point iterations with parameters shared across iterations that mimic an infinite-depth network; it matches benchmarks at much-reduced complexity, and the number of forward iterations can follow users' computation capability. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-11-28.
- [Path Independent Equilibrium Models Can Better Exploit Test-Time Computation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09961): In equilibrium models, upward generalization to harder instances with more test-time iterations correlates with path independence (reaching the same fixed point from any initialization); promoting it improves generalization and penalizing it degrades it. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-11-18.
- [MiniALBERT: Model Distillation via Parameter-Efficient Recursive Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.06425): MiniALBERT distills fully parameterised LMs such as BERT into a compact recursive student that reuses one shared Transformer layer at every iteration, optionally with per-iteration bottleneck adapters; students with no more than 18M parameters perform competitively on general and biomedical NLP tasks. Category: training; focus: related; 2022-10-12.
- [Stable Invariant Models via Koopman Spectra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07475): SIM describes the weight-tied, infinitely deep dynamics of DEQs via Koopman and Perron-Frobenius spectra, giving models trained like feedforward networks (single-tier SIMs use three transformations) that converge to a fixed point or a broader invariant set; SIMs match or beat DEQs on several tasks. Category: theory; focus: related; 2022-07-15.
- [Transformers discover an elementary calculation system exploiting local attention and grid-like problem representation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02536): A Universal Transformer with local attention over a grid-like memory and a PonderNet-style halting transformer learns multi-digit addition and place value alignment; trained on up to 4 operands of up to 10 digits, a variant reaches 0.99 sequence accuracy on 2-term additions of 1000-digit numbers. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-07-06.
- [Unveiling Transformers with LEGO: a synthetic reasoning task](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.04301): Introduces the LEGO chain-of-reasoning task and compares BERT with weight-tied ALBERT: trained on variables #0-#5, ALBERT reaches near-perfect accuracy on #6 and #7, probing shows it progresses more like a for-loop, and sampling depth between 6 and 12 during training further improves length extrapolation. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2022-06-09.
- [Representation Recycling for Streaming Video Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13492): StreamDEQ computes per-frame video representations as fixed points of an implicit (DEQ) network, starting each frame's fixed-point iterations from the previous frame's representation; on video segmentation, detection and pose estimation it matches the baseline's accuracy with 2-4x higher throughput. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-04-28.
- [Lightweight Bimodal Network for Single-Image Super-Resolution via Symmetric CNN and Recursive Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13286): LBNet pairs a parameter-shared Symmetric CNN with a Recursive Transformer whose two Transformer modules each feed their output back as input S times, for lightweight super-resolution; on Set5 ×4, recursing each module 2 times raises PSNR from 32.23 to 32.29 with parameters unchanged at 741.7K. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-04-28.
- [DRT: A Lightweight Single Image Deraining Recursive Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.11385): DRT builds a lightweight image-deraining Transformer from recursive blocks that reapply shared Swin Transformer blocks with residual connections; it uses only 1.3% of the parameters of the best-performing deraining model while beating state-of-the-art methods on Rain100L by at least 0.33 dB. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-04-25.
- [End-to-end Algorithm Synthesis with Recurrent Networks: Logical Extrapolation Without Overthinking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05826): Adds recall, which feeds the input into every iteration of a recurrent block, and a progressive loss over random iteration counts; together they prevent overthinking and let networks trained on small problems solve larger ones. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-02-11.
- [Deep Equilibrium Models for Video Snapshot Compressive Imaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.06931): Applies deep equilibrium models to video snapshot compressive imaging, computing the fixed point of a learned nonexpansive operator for unlimited iterations at constant memory; DEQ versions of an RNN and a Plug-and-Play reconstruction method are effective and stable on several datasets and real data. Category: applications; focus: related; 2022-01-18.
- [Universal Transformer Hawkes Process with Adaptive Recursive Iteration](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.14479): UTHP recursively applies one Universal Transformer encoding layer, with a CNN in its feed-forward part and modified ACT halting, to event sequences; it beats previous state-of-the-art point process models overall with fewer parameters, and ablations favor ACT over fixed iteration counts. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-12-29.
- [Sliced Recursive Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.05297): SReT shares weights across depth in vision transformers by looping each block; naive recursion gives a ~2% gain, and sliced group self-attention across recursions cuts the added cost by 10~30% with minimal performance loss. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-11-09.
- [The Neural Data Router: Adaptive Control Flow in Transformers Improves Systematic Generalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.07732): Neural Data Router adds a copy gate, which lets a column skip a step, and geometric attention to a Transformer with shared layer weights; it reaches 100% length generalization accuracy on compositional table lookup and near-perfect accuracy on simple arithmetic and a ListOps variant. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2021-10-14.
- [The Devil is in the Detail: Simple Tricks Improve Systematic Generalization of Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12284): Revisits simple configuration choices, including Universal Transformer variants with weights shared across layers; a relative-position Universal Transformer reaches 85% on the PCFG productivity split versus 50% previously reported, and universal variants beat standard ones except on COGS and CFQ MCD 1. Category: understanding; focus: core; 2021-08-26.
- [Semantic Communication with Adaptive Universal Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.09119): Uses Universal Transformers with adaptive computation time halting as encoder and decoder of a semantic communication system; it reports higher BLEU and lower symbol error ratio than a fixed-depth Transformer system on noisy channels. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-08-20.
- [PonderNet: Learning to Ponder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05407): PonderNet runs a step function recurrently with a learned probabilistic halting policy; it outperforms earlier adaptive-computation methods on parity, succeeds at extrapolation, and matches state-of-the-art bAbI accuracy with less compute. Category: depth; focus: related; 2021-07-12.
- [Stabilizing Equilibrium Models by Jacobian Regularization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.14342): Regularizing the Jacobian of the DEQ fixed-point update stabilizes forward and backward convergence; on WikiText-103 a Pre-LN DEQ-Transformer that diverges without it reaches 24.5 perplexity, and DEQ-Transformer training time falls from 3.1× to 1.5× that of Transformer-XL. Category: training; focus: core; 2021-06-28.
- [Can You Learn an Algorithm? Generalizing from Easy to Hard Problems with Recurrent Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.04537): Trains weight-tied recurrent networks with few iterations on easy prefix-sum, maze and chess problems and shows that running extra iterations at test time lets them solve harder instances. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-06-08.
- [Staircase Attention for Recurrent Processing of Sequences](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.04279): Staircase attention runs a shared Transformer core chunk by chunk, carrying backward tokens so each token passes through the core N times (Ladder repeats it on the full sequence); at equal parameters it solves tracking tasks Transformers fail and lowers language-modeling and dialogue perplexity. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2021-06-08.
- [Lessons on Parameter Sharing across Layers in Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.06022): The paper builds an N-layer Transformer encoder-decoder from M independent layers assigned by sequence, cycle or cycle (rev), relaxing Universal Transformers' one-layer sharing; on WMT English-to-German with M=6 and N=12, all three train faster than Universal Transformers with slightly better BLEU. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2021-04-13.
- [JFB: Jacobian-Free Backpropagation for Implicit Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.12803): JFB trains implicit networks, which infer by solving a fixed-point equation, by omitting the Jacobian term from backpropagation, keeping training memory fixed; on MNIST, SVHN and CIFAR-10 they are competitive with feedforward and prior implicit networks of the same parameter count. Category: training; focus: related; 2021-03-23.
- [Perceiver: General Perception with Iterative Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.03206): Perceiver repeatedly cross-attends from a small latent array to large inputs, with weights shared across repeats after the first, like an RNN unrolled in depth; it is competitive across images, point clouds, audio and video. Category: applications; focus: related; 2021-03-04.
- [On the Theory of Implicit Deep Learning: Global Convergence with Implicit Layers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.07346): For deep equilibrium models with nonlinearity only on weights, proves that gradient dynamics reach a global optimum at a linear rate without width assumptions, and relates them to trust region Newton on a shallow layer. Category: theory; focus: related; 2021-02-15.
- [Of Non-Linearity and Commutativity in BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04547): Analyzing BERT, the paper finds its layers largely commutative, mainly due to skip connections; ALBERT-like models that repeat one fine-tuned layer 12 times fall to random guessing but improve after 3 more fine-tuning epochs, which the authors take as support for recurrent and weight-shared Transformers. Category: understanding; focus: related; 2021-01-12.
- [Subformer: Exploring Weight Sharing for Parameter Efficiency in Generative Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00234): Subformer shares parameters across the central layers of generative Transformers, with unshared first and last layers and self-attentive factorized embeddings; it can beat the Transformer on translation, summarization and language modeling with fewer parameters. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2021-01-01.
- [Implicit Feature Pyramid Network for Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.13563): i-FPN replaces a detector's stacked cross-scale FPN blocks with the fixed point of one weight-shared transformation, solved DEQ-style with a residual-like iteration; on MS COCO it adds +3.4, +3.2, +3.5, +4.2, +3.2 mAP to ResNet-50-FPN RetinaNet, Faster-RCNN, FCOS, ATSS and AutoAssign. Category: applications; focus: related; 2020-12-25.
- [Multiscale Deep Equilibrium Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08656): MDEQ solves for and backpropagates through the equilibrium points of several feature resolutions at once, using implicit differentiation with O(1) memory; on ImageNet classification and Cityscapes segmentation it matches or exceeds competitive vision models. Category: applications; focus: related; 2020-06-15.
- [Monotone operator equilibrium networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08591): Introduces monDEQ, an implicit-depth model built on monotone operator theory whose parameterization guarantees a unique equilibrium, solved with operator-splitting methods that converge stably; it outperforms Neural ODE-based models while being more computationally efficient. Category: theory; focus: related; 2020-06-15.
- [RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12039): RAFT builds all-pairs 4D correlation volumes and iteratively updates a flow field with a weight-tied recurrent update operator; it reaches 5.10% F1-all error on KITTI and 2.855 pixels end-point error on Sintel (final pass). Category: applications; focus: related; 2020-03-26.
- [Addressing Some Limitations of Transformers with Feedback Memory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.09402): Feedback Transformer makes every layer attend to per-timestep memory vectors that mix all layers' past representations, exposing high-level past states to low layers; small, shallow models beat comparable Transformers on language modeling, translation and RL. Category: architecture/state; focus: core; 2020-02-21.
- [Neural Execution of Graph Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.10593): Trains graph neural networks to imitate each step of classical graph algorithms by repeating an encode-process-decode network with a learned termination network; max-based message passing works best, and learning reachability alongside improves shortest-path learning. Category: applications; focus: related; 2019-10-23.
- [ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning of Language Representations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11942): ALBERT reduces BERT's parameters with a factorized embedding and cross-layer parameter sharing, adds an inter-sentence coherence loss, and sets new state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE and SQuAD with fewer parameters than BERT-large. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2019-09-26.
- [Deep Equilibrium Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.01377): DEQ finds the fixed point of a weight-tied layer by root-finding and backpropagates through it implicitly; on language modeling such as WikiText-103 it often beats similar-size models while cutting memory by up to 88%. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2019-09-03.
- [Universal Transforming Geometric Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.00723): UTGN replaces the LSTMs of the recurrent geometric network with a Universal Transformer encoder whose 6-layer stack recurs up to 10 times with ACT halting; on CASP12 protein structure prediction it improves on RGN by 1.7 Å on free modeling and 0.7 Å on template based modeling. Category: applications; focus: related; 2019-08-02.
- [Latent Universal Task-Specific BERT](https://arxiv.org/abs/1905.06638): Latent Universal Task-Specific BERT replaces BERT's stacked self-attention blocks with one recurring three-layer block plus ACT, as in the Universal Transformer; on tweets the Universal Model has 46.3M parameters versus 110.1M for the base model, with masked LM accuracy 0.508 versus 0.507. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2019-05-16.
- [Attending to Mathematical Language with Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02825): On character-level evaluation of math expressions with symbolic variables, a standard Transformer, a Universal Transformer with recurrence and an adaptive Universal Transformer with recurrence and adaptive computation time reach test accuracies as high as 76.1%, 78.8% and 84.9%. Category: theory; focus: core; 2018-12-05.
- [Trellis Networks for Sequence Modeling](https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.06682): TrellisNet is a temporal convolutional network whose weights are tied across depth and whose input is injected into every layer, generalizing truncated RNNs; it outperforms the then state of the art on word- and character-level language modeling and long-term memory stress tests. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2018-10-15.
- [Recurrent Stacking of Layers for Compact Neural Machine Translation Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.05353): Shares parameters across all layers of an NMT encoder and decoder; a single layer recurrently stacked 6 times translates comparably to 6 separate layers, and back-translated data improves it further. Category: architecture/placement; focus: related; 2018-07-14.
- [Universal Transformers](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03819): Universal Transformer applies the same Transformer block recurrently over depth, with dynamic per-position halting; it is Turing-complete under some assumptions and outperforms standard Transformers on algorithmic and language tasks, gaining 0.9 BLEU on WMT14 En-De. Category: architecture/placement; focus: core; 2018-07-10.
- [Neural Ordinary Differential Equations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.07366): Neural ODEs replace discrete hidden layers with one network that parameterizes the hidden state's derivative, integrated by a black-box ODE solver; these continuous-depth models have constant memory cost, adapt their evaluation strategy to each input, and backpropagate scalably through any ODE solver. Category: applications; focus: related; 2018-06-19.
- [Early Improving Recurrent Elastic Highway Network](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.04116): EI-REHN adds an ACT-style elastic gate to Recurrent Highway Networks to set the recurrence depth per input, and a hypernetwork that updates intermediate-layer weights instead of sharing them; it beats other recurrent networks on synthetic regression, activity recognition and Penn Treebank language modeling. Category: depth; focus: related; 2017-08-14.
- [Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.08983): Introduces Adaptive Computation Time, a differentiable halting mechanism that lets an RNN learn how many steps to take per input; it improves performance on four synthetic tasks, while gains on character-level language modelling are small. Category: depth; focus: related; 2016-03-29.
- [Neural GPUs Learn Algorithms](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.08228): The Neural GPU repeats shared convolutional GRU layers for n steps on length-n inputs; trained with parameter sharing relaxation on up to 20-bit numbers, it adds and multiplies much longer binary numbers without errors. Category: applications; focus: related; 2015-11-25.
- [Deeply-Recursive Convolutional Network for Image Super-Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/1511.04491): DRCN applies a single convolutional layer recursively, up to 16 recursions, for image super-resolution, adding depth without new parameters; recursive-supervision and skip-connection ease training, and it outperforms previous methods. Category: applications; focus: related; 2015-11-14.

## Open questions

- [Does running more passes at test time than in training keep improving quality?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#extra-passes-at-test-time): mixed; Models trained with a sampled or variable number of passes stay flat or improve slightly beyond the training depth, and their gains level off near the training mean. Ouro, trained with 4 steps and learned exits rather than sampled depth, loses accuracy at 5-8 steps. No source trains the same model both ways, so the role of sampled-depth training is not isolated.
- [Where in the stack should the loop sit?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#loop-placement): consistent; Every comparison favors looping lower or middle layers over the whole stack or the top layers, and in layouts with a shared global KV the loop should include the layers that produce it. The comparisons come from models of 1.7B parameters or less (the 1.7B one finetuned from a pretrained model), or from runs whose sizes are not given.
- [With training compute held fixed, do more passes help?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#more-passes-fixed-compute): mixed; On language modeling at the budgets tested, SMELT and MoR find two passes better than three or four with FLOPs fixed, and in Ouro the gap to untied models of the same executed depth grows with the step count. Other results point the other way: Parcae's compute-optimal number of passes rises with the training budget, deeper training recurrence pays off per training FLOP for two of three retrofitted model families, and on Ouro's synthetic Mano task more passes of fewer layers win at the same executed depth.
- [Can later passes reuse one KV cache instead of keeping KV for every pass?](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/docs/en/questions.md#shared-kv-across-passes): mixed; Reusing the last pass's KV works when the model is trained for it or when it is done only during decoding, while reusing the first pass's KV alone costs accuracy unless a local window is added. Looped CED loses nothing with last-round KV under sampled-depth training but fails with fixed depth, Ouro keeps quality with last-step KV in decoding but not in prefill, and PLT needs a gated sliding window on top of first-pass KV sharing.

## Open models

- [Accordion-6B-A0.5B](https://huggingface.co/btzyd/Accordion-6B-A0.5B-RL): paper 2610.32492; 6.0B params; 3.6T, plus 50B at 32K context, then SFT and RL training tokens; passes 1 (loop_k 0); KV per-pass; license other (not named on the cards).
- [ALoDLM](https://huggingface.co/amazon/ALoDLM-8B): paper 2610.04198; 8B / 1.7B params; 5B-token SFT corpus (8 epochs at 8B) training tokens; passes up to 4, adaptive exit (max_depth 4); KV per-pass; license cc-by-nc-4.0.
- [ARLoop](https://huggingface.co/osunlp/ARLoop-1.2B): paper 2611.05234; 1.2B / 0.6B / 0.6B params; 500B / 180B / 180B training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Attractor](https://huggingface.co/jacobfa1/attractor-140m): paper 2605.12466; 140M / 370M / 770M params; 11.2B / 29.6B / 61.6B training tokens; passes 6-64, 6-64, 6-32 solver iterations (stops at tol); KV n/a; license mit.
- [Concertina-2.27B](https://huggingface.co/myboker/Concertina-2.27B): paper 2611.18113; 2.27B params; 22B (distilled from Qwen3-4B) training tokens; passes 2; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Depth-Recurrent Transformer (S1)](https://huggingface.co/joelogan/depth-recurrent-convergence): paper 2607.14427; 85.6M (state dict) params; 12.9B (12,900,106,240) training tokens; passes 8 (training mean; loops= is required per call); KV n/a; license mit.
- [DFM Mimir](https://huggingface.co/danish-foundation-models/DFM-Mimir-v1.5): paper 2608.13517; 1.787B params; 103B / ~70.5B per epoch (v1.5 / v1); total not stated training tokens; passes 8 module calls (H_cycles 2, L_cycles 3); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Dory1.0-4B](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Labs-Dory1.0-4B-BF16): paper 2611.03998; 4B params; 6T, plus 300B for context extension training tokens; passes 2; KV per-pass; license OpenMDW-1.1.
- [Foil (How to Loop MoE)](https://huggingface.co/ShourenWSR/how-to-loop-moe): paper 2609.35751; 553.7M each params; 100B each (FineWeb-Edu sample-100BT) training tokens; passes 16, 8, 4, 2 (Foil-1, Foil-2, Foil-3, Base; num_stacks); KV n/a; license apache-2.0.
- [GRT (Gated Recurrent Transformer)](https://huggingface.co/Amr-Hegazy/grt-medium-isoparam): paper 2608.15062; ~169M / ~358M / ~778M / ~287M params; ~9.8B each (CCCC Filtered) training tokens; passes 4, 4, 6, 6 (trained depth R; n is set per call); KV n/a; license cc-by-4.0.
- [HRM-Text-1B](https://huggingface.co/sapientinc/HRM-Text-1B): paper 2605.20613; 1B params; 40B unique, 60B in total training tokens; passes 8 module calls (H_cycles 2, L_cycles 3); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Huginn-0125](https://huggingface.co/tomg-group-umd/huginn-0125): paper 2502.05171; 3.5B params; 800B training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Inkling 2 Mini](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini): paper tml-inkling-2-mini; 26.4B params; not stated training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Intern-S2-Mobius](https://huggingface.co/internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius): paper 2608.14290; 35B params; 1TB tokens of continued pre-training (paper wording), then SFT and RL training tokens; passes 10 (40 layers share 4 routed-expert pools; layer i uses pool i mod 4); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Loop](https://huggingface.co/IQuestLab/IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Loop-Instruct): paper 2603.16733; 40B params; 12T+ pre-training and 600B mid-training (LoopCoder PDF) training tokens; passes 2; KV first-pass; license iquestcoder (Modified MIT License).
- [LatentLoop](https://huggingface.co/yhx12/LatentLoop): paper 2610.19975; 1.3B / 3B / 7B params; 40.0975B / 69.6538B / 139.7123B (reference budgets 40B / 70B / 140B) training tokens; passes 2 (middle layers visited twice, the first visit on a 2x compressed sequence); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [LoopCoder-V2](https://huggingface.co/Multilingual-Multimodal-NLP/LoopCoder-V2): paper 2606.18023; 7B params; 18T training tokens; passes 2; KV first-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Looped GPT-BERT 4x12](https://huggingface.co/Survivor613/BabyLM2026-Strict-Small-looped_GPT-BERT): paper 2609.09691; 12,181,780 params; 10 passes over 7,482,193 words (BabyLM 2026 Strict-Small) training tokens; passes 12 (num_loop_iterations); KV n/a; license not stated on the model card.
- [Looped UDLM (OpenWebText)](https://huggingface.co/saitejautpala/looped_udlm): paper 2610.30066; not stated (12 blocks, width 768) params; about 0.5T for the baseline; looped runs stop at matched training FLOPs training tokens; passes set per evaluation run: a fixed S or adaptive (cap 12); KV n/a; license apache-2.0.
- [LoopFormer](https://huggingface.co/armenjeddi/LoopFormer-3block-8iterations): paper 2602.11451; 278,169,600 / 223,635,456 / 278,169,600 (safetensors) params; ~25B (deduplicated Pile) / ~25B / not stated training tokens; passes 8, 12, 8 (steps); KV n/a; license not stated (no model cards).
- [Loopie-20B-A2B-preview](https://huggingface.co/zitian-gao/Loopie-20B-A2B-preview): paper 2607.16051; 20B params; 3.5T (pretraining) training tokens; passes 2 (layer_loop_times); KV per-pass; license mit.
- [Loopie-6B-A0.6B-preview](https://huggingface.co/zitian-gao/Loopie-6B-A0.6B-preview): paper 2607.16051; 6B params; 3T pretraining + 1.26T annealing (paper Section 3) training tokens; passes 2 (layer_loop_times); KV per-pass; license mit.
- [LoopUS](https://huggingface.co/Thrillcrazyer/Qwen3_1.7B_LoopUS): paper 2605.11011; 1.7B / 1.7B / 4B / 8B / 14B / 1.1B params; 3B (FineWeb-Edu) each; the SFT repo adds UltraChat 200k training tokens; passes up to 20 (config N; 100 for the 4B), confidence exit; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [LoopVL-1B](https://huggingface.co/TierFlow/LoopVL): paper 2609.38426; 1B params; 0.14T across all stages (75B text pretraining) training tokens; passes H2L3: [L×3→H]×2, 128 layer calls; KV n/a; license not stated on the card (repo includes LICENSE-Penguin.txt).
- [Metis-1.6 Logos](https://huggingface.co/Lernex/Metis-1.6-Logos): paper 2610.37903; 10.23B params; 804.76B pretraining; 1,022.70B with context extension and SFT training tokens; passes 2; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Metis-1.6 Praxis](https://huggingface.co/Lernex/Metis-1.6-Praxis): paper 2610.37903; 2.94B params; 804.76B pretraining; 1,022.77B with context extension and SFT training tokens; passes 2; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Nanbeige4.2-3B](https://huggingface.co/Nanbeige/Nanbeige4.2-3B): paper 2607.22083; 4B (3B non-embedding) params; 28T (pretraining) training tokens; passes 2 (num_loops); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [OrbitLM-1.8B-Thinking](https://huggingface.co/ai-forever/OrbitLM-1.8B-Thinking): paper 2610.00673; 1.86B params; 1.5T (1.48T in the paper), plus 14.7B SFT and RL training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Ouro-1.4B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance/Ouro-1.4B): paper 2510.25741; 1.4B params; 7.7T training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Ouro-2.6B](https://huggingface.co/ByteDance/Ouro-2.6B): paper 2510.25741; 2.6B params; 7.7T training tokens; passes 4; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Parcae](https://huggingface.co/SandyResearch/parcae-140m): paper 2604.12946; 140M / 370M / 770M / 1.3B params; 11.2B / 29.6B / 61.6B / 104B training tokens; passes 8; KV per-pass; license not stated on the model cards.
- [PonderingPythia](https://huggingface.co/zeng123/PonderingPythia-1.4B): paper 2505.20674; 1.4B / 2.8B params; 300B (Pile) each training tokens; passes 4 per token (pondering_steps 3 + final pass); KV n/a; license apache-2.0.
- [PonderLM-2-Pythia](https://huggingface.co/zeng123/PonderLM-2-Pythia-1.4b): paper 2509.23184; 1.4B / 410M params; 300B (Pile) each training tokens; passes 2 per token (one latent thought); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-Llama-3.2 (4,6,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-Llama-3.2-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 851,501,056 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (Nemotron-CC-Math-v1) training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-OLMo-2-0425 (4,6,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-OLMo-2-0425-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 939,638,784 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (Nemotron-CC-Math-v1-4plus) training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [Recurrent-TinyLlama-3T (4,8,4)](https://huggingface.co/smcleish/Recurrent-TinyLlama-3T-train-recurrence-4): paper 2511.07384; 704,708,608 excluding embeddings (Table 8) params; about 50B (train-recurrence-k repos); 26B single phase, 52B two phase training tokens; passes 32; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [SenseNova-Loop-9B](https://huggingface.co/sensenova/SenseNova-Loop-9B): paper sensenova-loop-9b; approximately 9B params; not stated training tokens; passes 2; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [TaH-plus-1.7B](https://huggingface.co/nics-efc/TaH-plus-1.7B): paper 2511.08577; 1.76B (1.72B backbone + LoRA + decider) params; SFT on 100K Mixture-of-Thoughts samples (480M tokens) training tokens; passes up to 2 (per-token decider, threshold 0.9); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [TaH2-1.7B](https://huggingface.co/nics-efc/TaH2-1.7B-max2): paper 2609.35748; 1.7B backbone + 46.16M updater and decider params; 3.4B (3 epochs over 273K post-training samples) training tokens; passes up to 2, 4, 8 (max2, max4, max8; decider threshold 0.5); KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.
- [TML-d24-varloop-research](https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research): paper tml-inkling-2-mini; 26.4B params; not stated training tokens; passes 3; KV per-pass; license apache-2.0.

## Data

- [papers.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/data/papers.json): every paper entry (deep and radar) as JSON
- [models.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/data/models.json) and [claims.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/data/claims.json)
- [metrics](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/data/metrics/latest.json): citations, stars, Hugging Face upvotes and downloads
- [schema](https://github.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/tree/main/schema): field definitions and allowed values
- [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sjy1203/awesome-loop/main/llms-full.txt): all English deep cards in one file
